findings.title: Down-side re-entry is keyed on the Up book's timestamp, throttling half the strategy
findings.claim: The same-book-snapshot dedup uses m.book_us (Up-token book clock) for BOTH sides, but Down fires are sourced from the Down token's own book whose clock is m.book_dn_us. After any fire in a market, new Down asks arriving as Down-book deltas (which update book_dn_us, not book_us) are rejected as 'same book snapshot' until an unrelated Up-book event happens; conversely an Up-book tick re-unlocks the SAME unchanged resting Down ask (bounded only by the claimed-vs-printed ledger).
findings.evidence: bot/strategy.py:240-243: `if self.last_book.get(m.slug) == m.book_us:\n    self.f["cooldown"] += 1\n    return None  # same book snapshot; would be a fictional second fill` — and the key is set identically for both sides at :280 and :293 (`self.last_book[m.slug] = m.book_us`). bot/state.py:685-691 shows Down events update only book_dn_us: `if m.asset_id_dn == asset_id: m.apply_delta(False, ...); m.book_dn_us = now_us()`.
findings.failure_scenario: z <= -2 in a 5m settle window; the losing Up token goes one-sided and static (the exact state described at strategy.py:209-214: 'the losing token loses its bid and quotes 0.001'). First Down fire records book_us=X. Fresh Down asks then stream in on the Down book (the code's own measurement: a qualifying market prints a median ~1,291 shares in-window and one entry captured only ~40, which is why re-entry exists, strategy.py:168-180) — every one is refused at line 240 because book_us is still X. The Down side is throttled to the Up book's event rate, exactly the 'timer cooldown suppressed 867 of 1,681 evaluations' failure (strategy.py:176-180) reintroduced for one whole side; in the older combined log Down was 150 of 340 fills, so this suppresses roughly half the signal surface in paper AND live. The reverse direction also holds: any Up-book delta unlocks a duplicate take of the unchanged Down ask (print-ledger-bounded fictional fills). Note run.py:761 has the same asymmetry — staleness gates check only (now - m.book_us), so a frozen Down book passes the 10s book-age check on the Up book's freshness.
findings.fix: Key the dedup on the book the candidate ask actually came from: for Down with dn_src=='book' compare/store m.book_dn_us (separate last_book entry per (slug, side)); for Up and for the mirror fallback keep m.book_us. Pass book_dn_us into the risk book-age check when trading off the real Down book.

findings.title: Strike latch races the oracle's ~1.6-2.8s delivery lag, freezing a wrong K forever
findings.claim: strike_avg latches k_fixed the first time it is called with now_us() >= t0, but Chainlink rounds arrive well after their round timestamps (measured on data/live/rtds: p50 1.62s, p90 2.09s, p99 2.47s, max 2.80s delivery lag, round stamps second-aligned). Any call landing in [t0, t0+~2.5s] latches K permanently missing the last 1-3 ticks of the [t0-w, t0) strike window, with the hold-integral silently extrapolating an older price over the gap.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:638-639: `if now_us() >= m.t0_us:\n    m.k_fixed = ps / secs            # window closed: latch it`. Measured from data/live/rtds/2026-08-09_23 + 2026-08-10_00 jsonl (btc/usd, n=1102): payload round ts 1786320303000 (ms) received at t_local_us 1786320304144651, delivery lag p50 1.623s / p99 2.471s. The caller that hits this window is the 30s health loop (run.py:562 `await asyncio.sleep(5 if first else 30)`; run.py:568 `"K": (round(s.strike_avg(m), 2) ...)`), so ~2.5/30 ≈ 8% of markets latch inside the race window.
findings.failure_scenario: Health tick fires at t0+0.8s for a market whose strike-boundary second moved 3 sigma (exactly the regime this bot trades). The final ~2s of the strike window are held at the pre-move price, so K is off by (2/30)*delta. In z units the numerator error is tau*delta = 2s * 3*sigma_1s against a denominator sigma*sqrt(rem^3/3): ~0.9 z at rem=5s, ~2.0 z at rem=3s — enough to flip the z>=2 gate in either direction for the whole settle window. Because _settle_result also reuses the cached wrong m.k_fixed, the in-process paper grade shares the error and hides it; only Gamma scoring (score_paper.py) reveals the loss.
findings.fix: Latch only when now_us() >= m.t0_us + LATCH_GRACE_US with grace ~3.5s (> measured max delivery lag), or re-latch if a tick with round ts < t0 arrives after the first latch. Pre-latch reads already recompute correctly, so the grace costs nothing.

findings.title: _settle_result coverage guard is vacuous: settle grade back-extrapolates over feed gaps
findings.claim: settle_sum_so_far discards the `covered` and n_ticks quality flags that _integral returns, and run.py's only guard (`r_secs < m.w * 0.9`) can never trip unless the window has ZERO ticks, because _integral always returns secs = (b-a)/1e6 when any tick exists — so a settle window with one late tick and a multi-second oracle outage is graded as fully known, with the first tick's price back-extrapolated over the uncovered head and held prices over the gap.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:646-647: `ps, secs, _, _ = self._integral(m.t1_us - w_us, min(t_us, m.t1_us))\nreturn ps, secs` — flags dropped. bot/state.py:596: `return total / 1e6, (b_us - a_us) / 1e6, len(pts), covered` — secs is the full span regardless of coverage; only the no-tick case (state.py:586-587) returns 0. run.py:235: `if K is None or r_secs < m.w * 0.9: return None`. Contrast strike_avg, which correctly requires `secs <= 0 or not covered or nticks < 3` (state.py:636).
findings.failure_scenario: Position taken at rem=25s; the RTDS socket dies at t1-20s and reconnects at t1-4s. The real oracle kept printing (and the venue settles on those prints), but the bot's ring buffer holds a t1-20s price across 16 of the 30 settle seconds. _settle_result computes r_secs=30, passes the 0.9w guard, and grades the fill on a fabricated average — feeding risk.on_settle_pnl and the daily-loss kill switch with a possibly sign-flipped P&L (per findings 9.6 the same machinery already mismatches the venue ~0.7% on btc even with good coverage). The headline +4.55c is Gamma-scored by src/score_paper.py so it is not contaminated, but the in-process kill switch and day_pnl seeding are.
findings.fix: Return and check the quality flags: in _settle_result require covered, nticks >= ~0.5*w*observed tick rate, and max intra-window gap below a few seconds; otherwise defer to the Gamma fallback that settle_loop already has.

findings.title: Calibration table bakes a 3-day up-drift: 8-12pt Up/Down asymmetry under a symmetric gate
findings.claim: The empirical z->P(Up) table is strongly asymmetric — at |z|=2.5 the favoured side wins 0.8878 when it is Up but only 0.8083 when it is Down (1-0.1917), and the skew is 8-12 points at every |z| — yet the bot gates both sides with the same zmin=2.0 and the same max_price=0.99. Measured on only 2026-08-07..09, the asymmetry is most plausibly sample drift (an up-trending window), so fair() hardcodes a 3-day regime into every ev_est and into the require_edge path; no per-side EV split of the +3.04c validation is published anywhere even though endgame_rollavg.py labels sides.
findings.evidence: bot/calib.py:20-31: POINTS = [(-3.5, 0.1833), (-2.5, 0.1917), (-1.5, 0.2860), ... (2.5, 0.8878), (3.5, 0.9159)] — P(Down|z<=-3.5)=0.8167 vs P(Up|z>=3.5)=0.9159; at ±1.5, 0.8382 vs 0.7140. bot/state.py:747-749 makes this the fair value: `z = self.zscore(m, t_us); emp = _p_up(z); return gauss if emp is None else float(emp)`. src/endgame_rollavg.py:132-146 carries a side column but no per-side EV appears in reports/findings.md.
findings.failure_scenario: By the bot's own table, a Down fill at ask 0.90 with z=-2.5 has EV = 0.8083 - 0.90 - 0.0063 fee = -9.8c/share, while the identical Up-side trade reads -1.9c — yet both pass the identical gate up to 0.99. If the pooled +3.04c is carried mostly by the Up leg, the live book runs a hidden losing Down leg at high asks; if instead the asymmetry is drift, then in a down-trending week the Up rows (measured in an up-drift) overstate Up win probability by ~8-10pts and every logged ev_est (and require_edge, if ever enabled) is wrong in the dangerous direction. Either branch is checkable in an hour from the existing prints data and neither has been checked.
findings.fix: Publish the per-side (Up vs Down) c/share and hit-rate split of the |z|>=2 validation before live; if the asymmetry is real, gate Down with a lower max_price or higher zmin; if it is drift, recalibrate the table on a longer, drift-balanced sample (or fit symmetric |z| buckets).

findings.title: require_edge threshold ignores the taker fee it is supposed to clear
findings.claim: The optional edge gate compares fv - ask against edge_min=0.02 with no fee term, although the venue fee 0.07*p*(1-p) is ~1.75c at mid prices — so the gate's real net-EV floor is ~0.3c, not the 2c the config name implies; the fee-aware ev_of() sits two lines above it and is used only for logging.
findings.evidence: bot/strategy.py:255-256 defines `def ev_of(fair, ask): return fair - ask - 0.07 * ask * (1 - ask)` but the gate at :276 is `if self.require_edge and fv - ba < self.edge_min: return None` (and :289 for Down) — no fee. Config note (bot/config.json rollavg_edge) says require_edge fires at avg px 0.389, where the fee is 0.0166, i.e. 83% of edge_min.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone flips require_edge=true to run the measured-clean variant (the config note explicitly keeps it as a paper-measurement flag): trades with fv - ask in [0.020, 0.037) at mid prices pass the gate with net EV between -1.7c and 0 after fee, diluting the +10.15c/share the flag was measured to deliver and corrupting the comparison the flag exists to make.
findings.fix: Gate on ev_of(fv, ba) >= edge_min (and ev_of(1-fv, ask_dn) for Down), i.e. subtract the fee inside the threshold, matching how the +10.15c figure should be defined.

findings.title: Down pricing never takes the cheaper of the real Down ask and the Up-bid mirror
findings.claim: best_ask_dn (and depth()) return the real Down-book ask whenever one exists and consult the 1-best_bid_up mirror only when the Down book is empty — but Polymarket's CLOB crosses a Down buy against complementary Up bids via minting, so the executable Down price is min(real_dn_ask, 1-bb_up). When the real Down book quotes wide (e.g. 0.995) while a thick Up bid implies 0.985, the max_price=0.99 gate rejects a trade that is actually executable, and fills are priced off the worse source.
findings.evidence: bot/state.py:267-274: `if self.asks_dn:\n    return self.asks_dn[0] + ("book",)\nbb, bbs = self.best_bid() ... return (round(1.0 - bb, 4), bbs, "mirror")` — unconditional preference; depth() at :286-294 has the same either/or structure and never merges the two ladders.
findings.failure_scenario: Config's own numbers: the 0.985-0.990 band holds 1.22M of 2.6M qualifying shares at +0.57c/share. Every settle-window snapshot where the real Down ask sits at 0.995+ while the Up bid implies <=0.99 is a rejected-but-executable trade in exactly that band; merging the two sources (min for the gate, interleaved ladders for depth) recovers that volume at no model change and strictly improves every accepted Down price.
findings.fix: In best_ask_dn return the minimum of the real Down ask and round(1-bb,4) (with its size), and have depth('Down', limit) merge both ladders sorted by price; keep dn_src for attribution.

result.clean_areas: Derived the contract math independently and verified the implementation term by term — the core is correct: (1) z algebra: phase-3 A|F_t ~ N((R+P_t*rem)/w, sigma^2*rem^3/(3w^2)) gives z=(R+spot*rem-K*w)/(sigma*sqrt(rem^3/3)), exactly state.py:775-777 and rollavg_pricer.py:92-96; phase-2 variance s+w/3 re-derived via the double integral of min(u,v) and matches state.py:772-773; the two branches are continuous at rem=w. Units are consistent throughout (numerator price-seconds, sd $*s). (2) Window boundaries: strike uses _integral(t0_us-w_us, t0_us) and settle uses _integral(t1_us-w_us, min(t,t1_us)), both half-open [a,b) with a tick at exactly a treated as in-force and a tick at b excluded — matches [t1-w,t1)/[t0-w,t0); tie-break `>= K` gives ties to Up per contract (run.py:237). (3) Timestamp units verified end-to-end against recorded data: RTDS payload timestamps are ms, second-aligned, strictly monotone with no duplicates in the sample (n=1102); run.py passes ms to on_oracle which stores us; backfill's *1000 matches; Binance T handled in ms with a us guard; vol.update gets ts_ms//1000 seconds correctly. (4) The S-vs-K gap asymmetry the brief warned about does not exist: BOTH averages come from the same time-weighted hold integral (_integral), so missing oracle seconds are handled symmetrically, and the count-vs-elapsed-seconds confusion (sum-of-ticks scaling) is fixed by integrating; observed-portion R plus spot*rem covers exactly w seconds against K*w. (5) sigma: sigma_rel is the oracle's own 1s log-return sd using only adjacent-second pairs (correctly avoiding sqrt(gap) inflation), multiplied by spot at the single right place (state.py:740, 769); the Binance fallback guard is complete — cold start with no oracle reference refuses to price, and the 3x band vs the last good oracle reading blocks the documented 5x under-read; memoization is per-second and harmless. (6) 15m family: m.w=60 is set from market duration, the gate min(window_s=60, m.w) yields 30s/60s correctly, and no 30 is hardcoded in the trading path. (7) min_rem_s floor and window-entry transition behave continuously; settle grading at t1+10s is complete given the measured max 2.8s delivery lag. (8) Fee formula 0.07*p*(1-p) matches venue facts in ev_of; Up/Down gates test the correct side's own ask (real Down book preferred, mirror as fallback with correct 1-bb arithmetic and correct mirrored print accounting). (9) Verified the headline +4.55c is scored against the venue's Gamma outcomes by src/score_paper.py, not by the bot's self-grading, so the paper result is not circular. (10) Checked the discrete-hold (jump-process) vs continuous-BM variance question at small rem: the continuous rem^3/3 overstates variance ~8-60% for rem<=5s, but the empirical p_up calibration and the z>=2 gate were both measured with the same formula, so the pipeline is self-consistent and the bias is conservative (misses late signals rather than manufacturing them) — not reported as a defect.

findings.title: Tape caps count opposite-direction and wrong-token prints: ~2x fill-size inflation
findings.claim: printed() — the sole evidence base for cap_tape and cap_life — filters prints only by price, never by aggressor side or economic direction. The tape merges both tokens (run.py:471 'if mirror: px = 1.0 - px') and run.py:468-474 discards the ev['side'] field the feed provides (verified present: all 570 recorded last_trade_price events carry side, 508 BUY / 62 SELL). With config max_price=0.99 the price filter passes essentially every print in the market (<=0.99 for Up buys, >=0.01 mirrored for Down buys), so prints of people SELLING into bids and of takers buying the OPPOSITE token are counted as volume our taker BUY could have won. Measured on the local capture (570 prints, 7 markets): counted/direction-correct volume = 2.0x aggregate, median 2.0x per market-token, p75 6.0x, max 21x, where direction-correct = BUY prints on the bought token + SELL prints on the complement (mint-cross supply). audit.md:24-25 shows the both-token merge was deliberately MATCHED to the tape backtest — meaning the $/day capacity projections inherit the same inflation; consistency with the backtest is not consistency with live FAK fills, which can only win same-direction flow.
findings.evidence: state.py:326-331: 'for t_us, px, sz in reversed(self.tape): ... if side == "Up": if px <= limit + 1e-9: tot += sz / elif px >= (1.0 - limit) - 1e-9: tot += sz' — no side test. run.py:468-474: 'elif et == "last_trade_price": px = float(ev["price"]); sz = float(ev.get("size", 0)); if mirror: px = 1.0 - px; self.state.on_trade(up_aid, px, ...)' — ev["side"] never read. Recorded event: '"price":"0.74","size":"1.35135",...,"side":"BUY"'.
findings.failure_scenario: Last 30s, z >= 2 says buy Up at ask 0.98 while the crowd is dumping: 100 shares of down-token BUY prints (people aggressively buying Down at 0.97-0.99, mirrored to up prices 0.01-0.03) plus up-token SELL prints land on the tape in 5s. cap_tape = 0.25*100 = 25 shares certified for our Up buy from purely opposite-direction flow; live, a FAK at 0.98 has zero of that flow available as counterpart. At the measured 2x aggregate inflation, everywhere the tape cap binds (per findings.md the 0.985-0.99 band holds 1.22M of 2.6M qualifying shares and is exactly where displayed depth is large so cap_tape governs), paper books ~2x the winnable size — the ~$2.4k booked and the $1.6-2.3k/day projection scale directly with that size. Caveat stated honestly: the capture covers rem 68-155s, not the settle window; in-window direction mix may differ, but any opposite-direction share is pure inflation.
findings.fix: Use the side field already in the feed: store (t_us, px, sz, taker_side, token) in m.tape; for a BUY of token X at limit L, count only BUY prints on X at px <= L plus SELL prints on the complement at complement-px >= 1-L. One-line change in _on_clob to pass ev['side'] through, and a two-branch filter in printed().

findings.title: cap_life ledger too dilute to stop double-dipping; effective participation ~5x intent
findings.claim: The 9fbc1bc fix for the known refresh-restore double-dip (consume() empties a level, the venue's next absolute-size delta or snapshot restores it) is cap_life = vol_participation * printed(side, limit, 0) - claimed, described in the code and commit as 'the binding realism cap'. It does not bind. printed(...,0) spans the market's WHOLE life (tape holds 400 prints; a 15m market has ~14 pre-window minutes of trading) and both directions (finding 1), while claiming only happens in the last 30-60s. Meanwhile cap_tape's rolling 5s window is re-armed by ANY book_us delta (strategy.py:248 gate; deltas arrive many times per second in the endgame — 49,962 price_change events in the ~85s recorded burst), so the SAME print justifies a fresh claim on every re-fire until it ages out: one print can be claimed ~5 times at vol_participation each, i.e. up to ~1.25x its size instead of 0.25x. The ledger only halts claims at 25% of whole-life two-direction volume, so in practice the per-market RISK caps (300 sh / $150) are what stop the paper broker, not any measure of winnable flow.
findings.evidence: run.py:693-695: 'cap_life = (f["vol_participation"] * m.printed(o["side"], o["limit"], 0) - m.claimed[o["side"]])'; run.py:684-686: 'cap_tape = f["vol_participation"] * m.printed(o["side"], o["limit"], now - int(f["vol_window_s"] * 1e6))'; state.py:219: 'self.tape = deque(maxlen=400)'; config.json: '"max_price": 0.99' makes the printed() price filter pass ~everything; strategy.py:248: re-fire allowed whenever book_us changed.
findings.failure_scenario: 15m market: 2,000 shares print pre-window, 500 in the settle window (~250 direction-correct). Intended cap: 0.25*250 = 62 shares. cap_life allows 0.25*2500 = 625; the $150 dollar cap binds first at ~153 shares @0.98 — a 61% effective participation in direction-correct flow, 2.5x the intended 25%. Concretely per print: a single 40-share print at 0.98 -> first fire claims 10; the level is restored by the next delta, book_us ticks re-arm the strategy, and 4 more fires inside the 5s window claim 10 each -> 50 shares booked off one 40-share print. The commit for the retroactive scorer (09c1469) concedes this decides 'whether the ~$2.4k/day run-rate projection was volume-inflated' — the forward-looking fix still leaves the same inflation live-vs-paper.
findings.fix: Make the ledger windowed and direction-aware: maintain per-side cumulative direction-correct printed volume since the market entered its settle window (or since first fire), and require claimed <= vol_participation * that quantity. That makes cumulative claims track contemporaneous winnable flow instead of lifetime both-direction volume, and subsumes the overlapping-window multi-count.

findings.title: Down-side re-fire gate keyed to Up-token book clock: same resting Down ask re-taken
findings.claim: The guard whose stated purpose is preventing 'a fictional second fill' on the same book state compares against m.book_us, which only up-token events update; Down-book quotes update m.book_dn_us (state.py:690). Both fire branches store m.book_us (strategy.py:294 and :306). In the settle window the up book ticks many times per second, so for Down signals taken from a real down book (dn_src=='book') the gate never suppresses: the identical resting down ask — whose consume() decrement is undone by every down-book refresh — is re-taken on every up-book delta, bounded only by the diluted caps of findings 1-2 and the risk caps. The gate is also wrong in the conservative direction: a genuinely new down ask arriving while the up book is quiet is suppressed as 'same book'.
findings.evidence: strategy.py:248: 'if self.last_book.get(m.slug) == m.book_us:' ... '# same book snapshot; would be a fictional second fill'; strategy.py:306 (Down branch): 'self.last_book[m.slug] = m.book_us'; state.py:686-690: up-token delta -> 'm.book_us = now_us()', down-token delta -> 'm.book_dn_us = now_us()'.
findings.failure_scenario: Down winning, z = -2.5, one MM rests 40 shares at 0.97 on the down book and never requotes. Up-token deltas tick ~5/s; each tick re-arms the gate, a new order queues, fires 410ms later against the refresh-restored 0.97 level, and consume() is undone by the next down-book snapshot. Subject to the tape caps passing (they do whenever any prints occur — finding 1 counts loser-side up prints toward Down buys), paper accumulates to the $150/market cap (~150 shares) off a single 40-share resting ask in a few seconds; live, one FAK takes at most the 40 (minus races) and subsequent FAKs find the level empty.
findings.fix: Track the gate per side and per book actually quoted: store (book_us if side=='Up' or dn_src=='mirror' else book_dn_us), or better, gate on the identity (price, size) of the specific ask targeted so an unchanged resting quote can never be ordered against twice.

findings.title: Delayed orders execute against arbitrarily stale books — no freshness check in _execute
findings.claim: _execute fills from m.depth() with no check of m.book_us / m.book_dn_us age. Book freshness is only enforced at SIGNAL time (risk.py:59 stale_book_s = 10.0 via inputs_ok), and the local book goes deliberately blind for the resubscribe gap every 240s cycle (run.py:403 't_end = time.time() + 240') and desyncs on queue-full drops (n_clob_drop) until the next full snapshot — snapshots are only ~2% of messages. A queued order firing during such a gap (via the 1s decide_loop) books a fill against a book that no longer exists; in the last 30s of a decided market, a several-seconds-old ask at <= 0.99 on the z-favoured side is usually already gone, so live FAKs would miss where paper fills.
findings.evidence: run.py:671: 'legs_avail = m.depth(o["side"], o["limit"])' — preceded only by the market-exists check and the flat reject draw; no recheck of book age anywhere in _execute. run.py:403: 't_end = time.time() + 240' (forced resub cycle); risk.py:59: 'self.stale_book_s = cfg.get("stale_book_s", 10.0)'.
findings.failure_scenario: Signal fires legitimately at book_age 0.2s, order queued; the clob ws hits its 240s cycle boundary and tears down; no deltas for ~1.5s; decide_loop's _process_pending executes the order at fire_us+~600ms against the pre-gap book showing 30 shares at 0.97 that were actually pulled during the gap. Roughly (gap ~1.5s / 240s) x (fraction of fires near a cycle boundary) of fills — order of 0.5-1% — are booked against vanished books, concentrated in fast markets where the miss would have been most likely. Low frequency, hence minor; the same one-line check also covers the n_clob_drop desync case, which is unbounded in duration.
findings.fix: In _execute, treat a stale view as the venue's re-validation reject: if now - (m.book_us if side Up/mirror else m.book_dn_us) > ~1.5s, count as ask_gone miss instead of filling.

result.clean_areas: TIMING (checked hard, correct): fills are never taken at decision time — taker signals queue with fire_us = now + (venue_hold_ms 250 + rtt_ms)*1000 and _execute runs against the book as of fire time or later (run.py:618-654), so realized cancels/decay/competing consumption up to T+~410ms are captured by construction; using the FULL rtt (not one-way) and executing at the first event/1s-tick at-or-after fire_us both bias conservative. The limit is the ask seen at decision, so price improvement is possible but marketability is re-tested against the delayed book (ask_gone miss otherwise) — faithful FAK+hold semantics. participation=0.5 is applied ON TOP of the delayed book as a race-share haircut, not as a substitute for survival, so the measured 63-69%/50% survival is not double-granted. reject_rate is drawn before sizing (run.py:666) — for a flat hazard the ordering is immaterial. UNITS/WALK: o['size'] is shares end-to-end (q_usd = size*limit confirms); the fill walks legs cheapest-first taking at most participation per level, books each leg at its own level price, logs true vwap, and broker cost = sum sh*(px + 0.07*px*(1-px)) matching the venue fee (paper.py:65-73) — no touch-price flattery, no unit mixups. MIN SIZE: want < 5 rejects the whole order after caps (run.py:698); the walk guarantees got == want, so no sub-5 partial can ever book; live's placement-time orderMinSize applies to the >=5-share order we would send, so paper is conservative here. SELF-COUNTING: paper fills are never appended to m.tape or fed back through on_trade_print — the tape is fed exclusively by venue last_trade_price events (run.py:468-474, state.py:694-701); no self-counting exists. DUAL-TOKEN DOUBLE PRINTS: tested on the recorded capture — 570 trades carry 570 distinct transaction_hashes with zero same-tx prints on both tokens of one market, so the mirror does NOT double-count a single match. CONSUME: within-burst double-spend is correctly prevented and depth()/consume() agree on which ladder (up asks, down asks, or mirrored up bids) is decremented, including the 4dp mirror rounding; a tape rolling off maxlen=400 can only shrink caps (conservative). EXPOSURE ACCOUNTING: in-flight orders count toward sizing and the opposite-side guard, and a kill/cool-off flushes the pending queue — no free fills after a stop. ADVERSE SELECTION (survival conditional on the signal being wrong): there is no accounting beyond flat participation, but this is explicitly disclosed as unmodelled in findings.md 8.6 and partly mitigated by construction since the sim fills off the real delayed book (realized conditional cancels are in the data); I attempted an empirical conditional test on data/live/books but the loser-side sample in the 0.92-0.99 band is n=6 snapshots — too thin to quantify locally (winner-side: 72% reachable / 90% size surviving at +400ms in 0.92-0.99, n=456; 51%/40% in 0.80-0.92, n=362). The new skip_px comment in strategy.py (live (0.95,0.98) band at -2.57c/sh vs +0.87c above) is consistent with residual adverse selection in the contested band; this remains a disclosed launch risk, not a new code defect. Data caveat for finding 1's measurement: the only local trade capture spans rem 68-155s (85s of prints), not the settle window, so the 2.0x direction inflation is measured out-of-window; the in-window mix may differ in either direction. NOTE: files changed mid-audit (commits 9fbc1bc..72060b7 landed from a parallel session); all findings and line numbers were re-verified against current HEAD 72060b7.

findings.title: Whole 536-market headline record predates the double-dip ledger; re-claims included
findings.claim: The +4.55c/share / $2.4k / 536-market record the launch rests on was produced entirely by the pre-9fbc1bc broker that could re-eat the same displayed liquidity after every book refresh, and neither score_paper nor status excludes or down-weights the possible re-claims; the fill-model-change reset policy (deploy/reset_pnl.sh) was not applied at 9fbc1bc.
findings.evidence: src/audit_doubledip.py:5-7: "The fills already on disk were taken WITHOUT that ledger, so the same displayed ask could be re-eaten after every venue book refresh". bot/run.py:690-692: "so without a lifetime ledger the same displayed liquidity can be eaten several times per market. This is the binding realism cap." Git dates: record reset bfb8024 2026-08-11 09:43; ledger fix 9fbc1bc 2026-08-12 10:24; the 9.6 aggregate quoting live 4.55c was committed edd3489 2026-08-12 10:18 — i.e. 100% of the quoted record is pre-ledger. deploy/reset_pnl.sh:8-9: "Mixing them into the same log means the scorer averages two incompatible fill models" — yet no reset accompanied 9fbc1bc.
findings.failure_scenario: If audit_doubledip's flagged fraction on the droplet is, say, 25% of shares, then booked P&L (~$2.4k), shares/market, and every $/day projection overstate deployable capacity by roughly that fraction — the live bot, running the ledger, will simply not get those fills. c/share and the market-clustered t are less exposed (re-claims fill at the same price in the same market), but total-$ tracking vs the $2,100/day projection will read as live underperformance that is actually paper over-crediting. Launch sizing calibrated on the blended record is calibrated on phantom liquidity.
findings.fix: Before go-live, run src/audit_doubledip.py on the droplet and make the 'clean' (first-claims-only) subset the launch decision number; either run deploy/reset_pnl.sh to start a post-ledger record, or add the re-claim flag as a default exclusion in score_paper/status so the headline is the ledger-consistent one.

findings.title: Clustered t assumes same-window markets independent; t=+4.13 is an upper bound
findings.claim: The headline t clusters on slug only, but the five coins' 5m markets in the SAME window settle on the same crypto-wide move (measured up_win correlation 0.52-0.65 across coins on 234k local settled markets), and at every :15 boundary a coin's 5m and 15m markets close together (67% outcome agreement). Five bots firing on one market-wide move are ~one bet, not five, so the market-clustered SE is understated and t=+4.13 overstated.
findings.evidence: src/status.py:101-109: g = sc.groupby("slug")... print(f"t = {tcl:+.2f} clustered by market (n={len(g)} markets..."); src/score_paper.py:251: "clustered by market (n={len(g)} markets)   <- the honest one"; src/tape_capacity.py:113-114 even mislabels the same slug-clustering as "t(day-clustered by market...)" though nothing clusters by day. Measured on data/pmfree_aug/meta (234,317 settled markets): cross-coin same-t1 5m up_win correlations btc-eth 0.653, btc-sol 0.585, btc-xrp 0.551, btc-doge 0.515; every 5m window lists all five coins; same-coin same-close 5m vs 15m agreement 0.6717 on n=4,359.
findings.failure_scenario: z fires when the final-window drift is large, which is disproportionately a market-wide move, so co-firing across coins is common. If ~30% of the 536 markets share their close window with one other traded market at outcome correlation ~0.57, the SE is understated ~8% (t 4.13 -> ~3.8); in the regime where all five coins co-fire on the same windows the cluster-sum variance inflates by (1+4*0.57) and t 4.13 -> ~2.3. The launch stat could sit anywhere in 2.3-3.8 instead of 4.13, and nothing in the code can tell you which.
findings.fix: Cluster on the close boundary: key = the t1 epoch in the slug (pooling coins and 5m/15m that share a close), or at minimum (t1, coin). Apply the same key in score_paper._report, status.pnl_by_bot and tape_capacity.clustered_t, and fix the false "day-clustered" label in tape_capacity.py:114.

findings.title: Maker fills invisible to default scoring and mis-charged a taker fee when included
findings.claim: paper.py books maker fills with no fee and emits them with no meta, so score_paper's default filters silently exclude every maker fill (empty reason fails reason_prefix, missing seen_px fails the latency filter, missing oracle_age_s fails the oracle filter), and when forced in with --reason-prefix '' --all-latency --all-oracle they are charged the taker fee they never paid via the fee_per_sh fallback.
findings.evidence: bot/paper.py:111-113: pos["cost"] += fill * o["level"] ... self._emit("maker_fill", oid=..., px=o["level"], shares=fill) — no fee, no meta. src/score_paper.py:148-156: reason/seen_px/oracle_age filters all read meta, which is {} for maker fills. src/score_paper.py:192: fee = float(f.get("fee_per_sh", FEE * px * (1 - px))) — fallback applies the taker formula to maker fills.
findings.failure_scenario: Currently latent (RollAvgEdge emits only taker_buy: bot/strategy.py:295,307; the maker strategies are disabled in config). But the day GzValueMaker/VacuumLadder or a rollavg maker variant is enabled, its entire P&L is invisible in the default status/score_paper headline — a maker strategy bleeding money would not appear anywhere — and any manual widened scoring mis-books it by 0.07*p*(1-p) (up to 1.75c/share near p=0.5) per fill.
findings.fix: Emit maker fills with meta (reason, oracle_age_s) and fee_per_sh=0.0 in paper.py, and make score_rows use fee_per_sh=0 for kind==maker_fill instead of the taker fallback.

findings.title: A voided/50-50 resolution is booked as Up total loss and Down total win
findings.claim: outcomes_for maps outcomePrices to a boolean with float(op[iu]) > 0.5, so a market the venue resolves 50/50 (refund at $0.50/share, the standard remedy for an oracle outage on these series) is booked as Up lost / Down won: Up fills take -px-fee instead of +0.50-px-fee, and Down fills take +1-px-fee instead of +0.50-px-fee.
findings.evidence: src/score_paper.py:64: out[m["slug"]] = float(op[iu]) > 0.5. Same test in the bot's own settlement fallback, bot/run.py:545: return 0 if float(op[iu]) > 0.5 else 1 — which additionally feeds risk.day_pnl and the kill switch.
findings.failure_scenario: A Chainlink stream outage voids a batch of 5m markets 50/50. A bot holding ~100 shares of Up at 0.97 in each is booked -97c/share when the true outcome is -47c/share; a Down holder is booked +2c when the truth is -47c. The record and day_pnl both mis-book by ~0.50/share in whichever direction, and the kill switch can trip (or fail to trip) on fictional numbers. Zero 50/50 outcomes observed in 234,317 local settled markets, so this is tail risk, not a current distortion.
findings.fix: Treat outcomePrices where max(op) < 0.99 as a distinct 'voided' status: book pnl = sh*(0.5 - px - fee) (fee treatment per venue refund policy) and count it separately in the report; same guard in run.py _gamma_result.

findings.title: No fill dedup key or fill-model stamp; record integrity rests on manual archiving
findings.claim: gather() concatenates logs/*/paper_fills.jsonl plus the legacy flat log with no per-fill identity (no dedup on slug/t_us/oid) and no broker-version stamp, so (a) any duplicated or restored file double-counts fills undetected, and (b) fills from the pre-0ca2161 broker (96% price-reach, 100% displayed size) pass every default filter — they carry seen_px and oracle_age_s — and are excluded from the headline only because deploy/reset_pnl.sh was manually run on 2026-08-11; the code cannot tell the eras apart.
findings.evidence: src/score_paper.py:119-121: logs = sorted(glob.glob("logs/*/paper_fills.jsonl")); if os.path.exists("logs/paper_fills.jsonl"): logs.append(...) — then lines 131-139 append every taker/maker fill line with no key. deploy/reset_pnl.sh:4-9: "Every fill before 0ca2161 was produced by a broker that reached its price 96% of the time... Mixing them into the same log means the scorer averages two incompatible fill models". Git: latency stamps default 53e1737 (Aug 11 06:13) predates the fill-mechanics rewrite 0ca2161 (09:38), so a multi-hour band of fills passes all default filters yet used the fictional broker.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator restores an archive (cp logs/archive/<stamp>/btc/paper_fills.jsonl logs/btc/ to 'look at old data'), or runs score_paper on a host where reset_pnl was never executed: the pre-cap fills silently blend into and inflate the headline c/share with no warning — exactly the 'meaningless blend' the reset script exists to prevent — or identical duplicated lines double every affected fill's weight.
findings.fix: Stamp meta with a fill_model version (bump at every broker-mechanics change) in paper.py._emit and default-filter score_paper to the current version; drop exact-duplicate (slug, side, t_us, px, shares) lines with a loud count when they appear.

findings.title: reset_pnl.sh: bot for a coin dropped from config keeps writing into the archive
findings.claim: The stop list is derived from the CURRENT bot/config.json coins, so a still-running unit for a coin since removed from config is never stopped; its open append fd follows the mv, so after the reset it keeps appending new fills into logs/archive/<stamp>/<coin>/paper_fills.jsonl — the live record silently loses that coin's fills and the archive gains post-reset fills, blending eras inside the archive. Separately, the final loop starts every configured unit unconditionally, including bots an operator had deliberately stopped.
findings.evidence: deploy/reset_pnl.sh:24-26: COINS=$(python3 -c "...get('coins',['btc'])"); UNITS=$(for c in $COINS; ...) — only these are stopped; line 36: mv "$src" "$DEST/${src#logs/}" (a running writer's fd follows the inode); lines 41-43: for u in $UNITS; do systemctl start "$u" ... — unconditional start.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator drops doge from config.json (edge went negative) but forgets to stop jsf-paperbot@doge, then runs reset_pnl.sh: doge trades on with all its fills landing in the archive — invisible to status.py/score_paper (glob depth excludes archive) — so a losing bot runs unmonitored indefinitely. Or: xrp was stopped pending its inverted-gap investigation; a routine paper reset restarts it. Live, that is unsupervised real-money trading.
findings.fix: Derive UNITS from running units (systemctl list-units 'jsf-paperbot@*') as well as config; record which units were active before stopping and start only those; after archiving, assert no process holds the archived files open (lsof).

result.clean_areas:
Settlement path (score_paper.outcomes_for): the known silent-100-slug-chunk-drop bug IS fixed and the fix is complete — 3 retries per chunk, still-failing chunks returned as a `failed` set, and both score_paper (lines 227-230) and status (lines 46-48) print them loudly as 'EXCLUDED... fetch failed, NOT still open'. I verified the `closed=true` + `outcomePrices > 0.5` decision empirically against live Gamma: a market that has closed but not resolved is NOT returned by a closed=true query (polled at t+3s..t+98s after close: absent; unfiltered query shows closed=False with live mid prices; once returned, outcomePrices are exactly ["0","1"]/["1","0"] with umaResolutionStatus=resolved) — so the >0.5 test only ever sees final 0/1 prices and 'unresolved (markets still open)' is truthful, apart from the theoretical 50/50-void case reported.

Fee: booked formula 0.07*p*(1-p) per share matches Polymarket's documented crypto taker formula (docs.polymarket.com: fee = C × feeRate × p × (1-p), feeRate 0.07 for crypto). Multi-leg taker fills are logged per leg at the real leg price with the fee computed at that leg's price (paper.py taker_fills lines 63-71), broker cost books px+fee at fill and pays 1.0 with no fee on settlement, and score_rows reproduces exactly that (sh*(won - px - fee), fee from the logged fee_per_sh) — winners and losers both pay fee on cost, never on payout, consistently in both places.

Double counting in the current layout: the archive directory cannot leak back into scoring (glob logs/*/paper_fills.jsonl is one directory deep; archives live at logs/archive/<stamp>/... two-three deep); the local flat legacy log's 185 rollavg taker fills all have seen_px=None and oracle_age_s=None so the default filters exclude them; per-coin logs and the flat log were never written concurrently for the same fill.

Open exposure: unresolved and fetch-failed fills are excluded from shares, avg px, hit, c/share, per-fill t, clustered t, run-rate and the by-price/by-coin tables (all computed on status=='scored' only), and surfaced as the 'open' column and the fetch-failed warning — nothing books them as wins or losses.

clustered_t (tape_capacity.py:58-74, score_paper.py:246-252, status.py:101-109): the share-weighting is implemented correctly (mu = total pnl / total shares; per-cluster residual pnl_g - mu*sh_g; sandwich SE), n is the number of MARKETS (groupby slug), and a market with 5 partial fills contributes one cluster; the naive per-fill t is still printed but explicitly labeled '<- WRONG, assumes fills are independent'. The only defect is the cluster KEY (cross-coin/cross-family same-window correlation), reported above. The missing G/(G-1) small-sample factor is ~0.1% at n=536 — immaterial.

Weighting consistency: avg px, hit rate and c/share are share-weighted identically in score_paper._report, status.pnl_by_bot per-coin and TOTAL rows, the by-family split, and audit_doubledip's blocks; the slippage line mixes a share-weighted mean with fill-count percentages but labels the latter 'of fills' explicitly.

reset_pnl.sh double-count check: archived fills cannot re-enter scoring; decisions.jsonl is archived alongside so run.py._seed_day_pnl (which re-sums only today's 'settled' lines from the per-coin decisions log) seeds day_pnl=0 after a reset — no orphan state re-enters either the scorer or the risk ledger. settle_loop's give-up path frees broker slots without deleting fills from the log, so scorer coverage survives bot-side settlement failure as designed.

findings.title: Settlement proceeds on a frozen oracle: the coverage guard is vacuous
findings.claim: _settle_result's only data-quality guard (r_secs < m.w * 0.9) can never fire when any oracle tick exists before the settle window, because _integral returns secs = (b_us - a_us)/1e6 unconditionally once 'covered' is true; the nticks and covered flags that would detect a frozen feed are computed by _integral but discarded by settle_sum_so_far. So markets settle off a price held from before a feed freeze, logged as src:'oracle', and the wrong pnl feeds risk.on_settle_pnl (day_pnl, streak breaker, probe).
findings.failure_scenario: A repeat of the observed 601s RTDS freeze spans two 5m markets holding positions. At t1+10s discover() settles both using the frozen pre-freeze price; if the real Chainlink path crossed K after the freeze, the result is inverted: winners booked as losers (and vice versa), day_pnl and the streak breaker are fed wrong outcomes — a false streak trip halts a healthy bot for 2h, or a real loss goes uncounted toward the $400 kill. The paper record used for the go/no-go silently diverges from the venue.
findings.fix: In _settle_result, use the full _integral return: require covered AND nticks >= 3 (matching strike_avg) AND the newest tick in oracle_hist to be >= t1 (or oracle_age_s() small); otherwise return None so the market defers to pending_settle and the authoritative Gamma fallback.

findings.title: Restart loses all position/exposure state; the fills log is never read back
findings.claim: On kill -9 / OOM / deploy restart, broker.positions, pending orders, pending_settle, and MarketState.claimed are all lost; PaperBroker opens paper_fills.jsonl append-only and nothing reads it back. _seed_day_pnl restores only risk counters. A restarted bot therefore sees zero shares in a market it already holds max size in and can buy the full per-market cap again; and fills from before the restart in markets that expire during the downtime never settle in decisions.jsonl, so risk.day_pnl permanently under-counts those losses.
findings.evidence:
paper.py:29-32: 'self.log = open(log_path, "a")
 self.orders = []
 self.positions = {}' — no read of the log anywhere (grep: no reader in bot/). run.py:112-119 seeds only risk: 'Rebuild today's realized P&L from the decision log on startup'. droplet_setup.sh:131-132: 'Restart=always
RestartSec=5' automates the re-entry, and restart_bots.sh restarts all five bots regardless of open positions.
findings.failure_scenario: Live: bot holds $150 (cap) of Up at 0.98 in a 5m market, crashes at rem=20s (e.g. the ENOSPC crash path or a slice OOM), systemd restarts it in 5s, z is still >= 2, it buys up to another $150 in the same market — 2x the stated max_market_dollars, with the first position invisible to every risk check and to the daily-loss accounting if the market expires before the process is back. In paper mode the same sequence writes cap-violating exposure into the record the capacity claims rest on.
findings.fix: On startup, replay the tail of paper_fills.jsonl (taker_fill/maker_fill minus settle lines) to rebuild broker.positions and per-market claimed for still-open markets; for the live build this becomes 'query venue positions before trading'. Gate go-live on this existing.

findings.title: Risk.seed cannot rebuild a probe kill: a deploy downgrades day-kill to 2h cooloff
findings.claim: seed() re-derives state only from (a) day_pnl vs daily_loss_limit and (b) the streak condition over today's outcomes. The killed=True set by a failed PROBE (risk.py:129-131, 'breakage confirmed: out for the rest of the UTC day') is not derivable from settle lines and is not reconstructed — so a restart while probe-killed resumes trading the same day. The docstring's claim 'a deploy cannot clear a tripped halt' (risk.py:40-41) is an incomplete fix.
findings.evidence: risk.py:146-161: seed() sets self.day_pnl, replays outcomes, then 'if self.day_pnl < -abs(self.daily_loss_limit): self.killed = True' and re-arms only the streak cooloff. No code path re-derives probe_losses_seen >= probe_losses. run.py:_seed_day_pnl logs the prior risk state string but nothing consumes it.
findings.failure_scenario: Venue re-prices (the exact event this bot's history contains): streak trips at 09:00, probe fails at 11:30, bot is killed for the day at day_pnl -$180. A routine restart_bots.sh deploy at 12:00 reruns seed(): -$180 > -$400, so killed stays False; at most a fresh 2h cooloff arms. At 14:00 the bot resumes trading a confirmed-broken edge and can bleed the remaining $220 to the backstop — per coin, since all five would be deployed together.
findings.fix: Persist the risk state transition (killed/halt/probe with reason and timestamp) as its own decision line and have seed() replay the most recent one for today; or simply re-run the full on_settle_pnl ladder over today's outcomes in order (which reproduces cooloff->probe->kill) instead of the two ad-hoc checks.

findings.title: z integrates held prices across feed-outage holes; no coverage check on integral
findings.claim: zscore() and fair() build the partial settle average S from _integral, which fills any gap in oracle_hist by holding the last price; nticks/covered are discarded (state.py:646-647). The 5s receipt-staleness gate blocks trading DURING an outage, and oracle_age_s<=20 bounds the current hole, but the moment the RTDS feed reconnects (recv timeout 15s + ~2s reconnect, run.py:330-337) both gates read fresh while the >=17s hole inside [t1-w,t1) stays in S until t1. The strike average K has the same exposure for holes in [t0-w,t0) and is then latched (k_fixed).
findings.evidence: state.py:775: 'r_sum, _ = self.settle_sum_so_far(m, t_us)'; state.py:777: 'return (r_sum + spot * rem - K * m.w) / sd'; state.py:592-596 holds cur_px across gaps: 'total += cur_px * (ts - cur_t)'; state.py:646-647 discards nticks/covered. run.py:287 'RECV_TIMEOUT_S = 15' then reconnect and resume with no backfill of the missed ticks.
findings.failure_scenario: RTDS goes silent at t1-30s, reconnects at t1-13s. The 17s hole contributes a held-price error to S with sd ~ sigma*sqrt(17^3/3) ~ $60 price-seconds (btc, sigma_rel 1.3e-5), against a remaining-signal sd of ~ $40 at rem=13 — a typical false shift of |z| by ~1.5 on a gate of 2. The bot fires at a 0.98-0.99 ask on a manufactured signal where a loss costs ~99c/share; at the $150 dollar cap that is up to ~$148 lost per contaminated market, on every outage that ends inside a settle window.
findings.fix: Track hole seconds: have settle_sum_so_far return max gap / uncovered seconds inside the window (from _integral's pts) and refuse to price (return None from zscore/fair) when the hole inside [t1-w, now) exceeds ~2-3s; additionally re-run backfill_oracle() on every rtds reconnect to repair the hole from the recorder's data/live/rtds capture, which is flushed to disk within ~50 ticks.

findings.title: No alerting anywhere, and a confirmed kill auto-resumes at UTC midnight
findings.claim: Every safety event is silent: kill switch, streak halt, probe kill, feed death, crash loop and unit-down produce only log lines that a human must fetch by running src/status.py manually. deploy/ has no OnFailure=, no notification hook, no watchdog (grep StartLimit|WatchdogSec|OnFailure over deploy/: no matches). _roll_day then clears killed at every UTC midnight, so a probe-CONFIRMED broken edge resumes trading daily with nobody told, bounded only by daily_loss_limit per coin per day.
findings.evidence: risk.py:101-112: 'if d != self.day: ... self.day_pnl = 0.0\n self.killed = False'; risk.py:129-131 sets the probe kill this clears. droplet_setup.sh defines all units with plain Restart=always and no OnFailure/alerting; status.py docstring: 'One-shot status' — a manual command.
findings.failure_scenario: The settlement rule changes again (it already did once, 2026-08-07, which is this project's founding event). All five edges invert. Each coin: streak trip -> 2h cooloff -> probe -> kill; at 00:00 UTC killed clears and the cycle repeats. Steady-state bleed up to $400/coin/day = $2,000/day aggregate, every day, until a human happens to run status.py. Live money makes this a launch blocker: the system is designed to be unattended but has no channel to say it is dying.
findings.fix: Add an ExecStart wrapper or a tiny alert loop: on kind in {settle_FAILED, killed transition, halts increment, rtds_round_stale, health gap > 2 min} send a push/email/webhook; add OnFailure=jsf-alert@%n.service to the unit templates; and require a manual re-arm (state file) after a probe kill instead of the midnight auto-clear, at least in live mode.

findings.title: Book staleness measured at processing time; queue lag and drops invisible to gate
findings.claim: on_book and on_price_change stamp m.book_us = now_us() at the moment the consumer processes the event and ignore the exchange timestamp (on_book's ts_ms parameter is unused). The stale_book_s=10 gate therefore measures time-since-processed, not book age: if the 50k clob queue backs up, or after a QueueFull drop leaves the level map desynced (run.py:421-427 only counts n_clob_drop, no forced resync until the next 240s resubscribe), stale books read as 0s old and pass inputs_ok. During each 240s resubscribe teardown the retained book also silently misses deltas for the ~1-2s gap while still passing the 10s gate.
findings.evidence: state.py:669-673: 'def on_book(self, asset_id, bids, asks, ts_ms):\n ... m.set_book(True, bids, asks)\n m.book_us = now_us()' — ts_ms never referenced; state.py:681-688 same for on_price_change. run.py:341 'queue = asyncio.Queue(50_000)'; run.py:426-427: on QueueFull only 'self.n_clob_drop += 1'.
findings.failure_scenario: A settlement-minute burst across 8-12 subscribed tokens outruns the Python consumer by 3-5s; the bot prices and paper-fills against asks that vanished seconds ago while book_age reads 0.1s — fills that live FAK orders would miss, inflating the paper record in exactly the last-30s regime the strategy trades. If the queue ever actually fills (the counter exists because it can), the book is wrong for up to 240s with a fresh-looking age.
findings.fix: Stamp book_us from the event's exchange timestamp (ev['timestamp'] is already delivered) or from an enqueue-time stamp; expose queue depth in the health line; on n_clob_drop > 0 break the subscribe cycle immediately to force a fresh snapshot.

findings.title: stale_binance_s is dead config: loaded, never enforced; spot_adj hardcodes its own 3.0s
findings.claim: The config key risk.stale_binance_s (3.0) is read into Risk but referenced nowhere else in the repo; inputs_ok deliberately dropped the Binance check, and the actual Binance freshness cutoff that decides whether spot comes from basis-adjusted Binance or the oracle is a hardcoded default parameter in state.spot_adj. An operator tuning stale_binance_s changes nothing.
findings.evidence: grep 'stale_binance_s' over *.py returns exactly one hit: risk.py:57 'self.stale_binance_s = cfg.get("stale_binance_s", 3.0)'. state.py:704: 'def spot_adj(self, max_binance_age_s=3.0):' with no caller passing the config value (state.py fair/zscore call self.spot_adj() bare).
findings.failure_scenario: Post-launch, Binance's public mirror degrades and the operator sets stale_binance_s to 1.0 to force the oracle path for spot — the change is silently ignored and z keeps being priced off a 3s-old basis-adjusted Binance print, while the config suggests the knob took effect.
findings.fix: Delete the key or wire it through: spot_adj(max_binance_age_s=self.risk.stale_binance_s) via a parameter on fair/zscore, and drop the unused attribute from Risk.

findings.title: RTDS watchdog behind symbol filter: missing coin stays down up to 600s
findings.claim: The rtds_feed round-age watchdog (MAX_ROUND_AGE_S=60, run.py:322) only executes after a message for THIS process's symbol arrives, because it sits below 'if pay.get("symbol") != self.state.oracle_symbol: continue'. If the multiplexed crypto_prices_chainlink stream keeps delivering other coins but drops ours (per-symbol upstream failure), the 15s recv timeout never fires and nothing forces a resubscribe until the CYCLE_S=600 rotation. Trading correctly stops at 5s receipt-staleness, but recovery that a reconnect would achieve waits up to 10 minutes.
findings.evidence:
run.py:311-322: 'if pay.get("symbol") != self.state.oracle_symbol:
 continue
 ...
 self.state.on_oracle(px, ts)
 ...
 if self.state.oracle_age_s() > MAX_ROUND_AGE_S:' — the age check is unreachable while our symbol is absent; run.py:288 'CYCLE_S = 600'.
findings.failure_scenario: Chainlink's doge/usd stream stalls upstream while btc/eth keep ticking. The doge bot idles (safe) but blind for up to 600s per occurrence instead of ~17s, forgoing 1-2 full markets each time; a recurring per-symbol outage pattern costs the thinner coins a measurable slice of their $158-$424/day.
findings.fix: Hoist the oracle_age_s() > MAX_ROUND_AGE_S check above the symbol filter (evaluate it on every received frame, or on a timer), so a reconnect is forced whenever OUR round is old regardless of which symbols are flowing.

findings.title: Daily loss limit counts settled P&L only; worst-case claim 2.5x understated
findings.claim: risk.day_pnl is updated exclusively via on_settle_pnl (run.py:212, 497), so open positions are invisible to the $400 stop; a coin can sit at -$399 settled with 4 x $150 = $600 more already committed across unsettled markets. Per-coin worst case is therefore ~$1,000, and the aggregate worst case is ~$5,000 — but the config's _per_process_note tells the operator the aggregate backstop is '$2,000'.
findings.evidence: config.json:25: 'a $2,000 daily backstop'; risk.py:115-119: on_settle_pnl is the only writer of day_pnl; risk.py:184: concurrency cap 'n_markets_with_pos >= self.max_concurrent' allows 4 markets x max_market_dollars=150 (config.json:9-10) of in-flight cost on top of the settled counter.
findings.failure_scenario: A correlated crypto flash move breaks all five coins in the same 15 minutes: each bot crosses -$400 settled with $600 still riding; realized aggregate day loss lands near $5,000 while the operator sized the account to the documented $2,000 backstop.
findings.fix: Either count committed cost toward the limit (day_pnl - open_cost < -limit blocks new signals), or correct the note to '$1,000/coin, $5,000 aggregate worst case' so live sizing is done against the real number.

findings.title: jsf.slice MemoryMax=900M below own measured peak; daily edge check forces reclaim/OOM
findings.claim: The setup script's comment records ~905MB steady for five bots + recorder and >1.1GB peak during the daily edge check, then sets MemoryHigh=700M / MemoryMax=900M on the very slice containing all of them. Even at the post-sklearn-fix footprint (~56MB/bot), edgecheck's own 600M allowance puts the group over 900M at 02:30 UTC daily: cgroup reclaim swaps the bots' pages out, stalling the asyncio loops of processes whose entire strategy lives in 30-second windows; if reclaim cannot keep up, the kernel OOM-kills the largest process in the slice.
findings.evidence: droplet_setup.sh:82-84: 'five bots plus a recorder measured ~905 MB with the daily edge check pushing the peak past 1.1 GB'; droplet_setup.sh:98-99: 'MemoryHigh=700M\nMemoryMax=900M'; droplet_setup.sh:186-189: edgecheck 'MemoryMax=600M' runs in Slice=jsf.slice at 02:30 UTC.
findings.failure_scenario: Daily at 02:30 UTC the group breaches MemoryHigh: every bot's pages are reclaimed to swap and its event loop stalls for seconds mid-settle-window — pending orders execute late against changed books and paper fills in that window are systematically mispriced; on a bad day the OOM killer takes a bot (usually edgecheck, but the victim is whichever task scores highest) and the position-loss restart finding follows.
findings.fix: Move jsf-edgecheck out of jsf.slice (its own 600M cap already bounds it), or raise the slice to MemoryMax=1200M now that the bots are 56MB each, and re-measure with systemd-cgtop as the comment itself instructs.

findings.title: Unguarded coroutines: one exception in settle/health/pending loops kills the process
findings.claim: main() gathers seven tasks with default semantics, so the first exception in any of them tears down the process. The feed tasks and _try_market are wrapped, but settle_loop's body (broker.settle + log writes), health_loop's body, and decide_loop's direct _process_pending() call are bare. A single OSError from a log write (log_decision and PaperBroker._emit both write+flush unguarded) — e.g. ENOSPC — becomes a full process death, then a permanent 5s crash loop: with RestartSec=5 against systemd's default StartLimitBurst=5/10s the limit never trips, and no StartLimit/OnFailure is configured in deploy/.
findings.evidence: run.py:877-881: 'await asyncio.gather(self.binance_feed(), ..., self.settle_loop())' — no return_exceptions; run.py:862-863 decide_loop: 'await asyncio.sleep(1.0)\n self._process_pending()' bare; run.py:487-519 settle_loop while-body has no try around broker.settle/log_decision; run.py:153-156 log_decision writes unguarded; grep StartLimit over deploy/: no matches.
findings.failure_scenario: Disk fills (recorder burst before the 20-min pruner runs): the next decisions.jsonl write raises ENOSPC, the process dies, systemd restarts it every 5s forever, each restart re-running _seed_day_pnl (32MB read) and seed_vol (4 Binance HTTP calls) and losing all position state — five coins simultaneously, silently, until a human notices trading stopped.
findings.fix: Wrap the bodies of settle_loop/health_loop and decide_loop's _process_pending in the same try/log pattern as _try_market; make log_decision swallow-and-count OSError; add StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst plus OnFailure alerting so a genuine crash loop becomes visible instead of infinite.

findings.title: Restart within hours of a streak halt re-arms a fresh full 2h cooloff
findings.claim: seed() re-checks the streak condition against today's full outcome list and, if >= 6 losses sit in the last 20, arms halt_until_us = now + cooloff_s — regardless of how much of the original cooloff was already served or whether the probe had already passed. Since on_settle_pnl clears self.recent at trip time but the log retains every outcome, the 6 losses remain visible in the tail for hours, so every deploy in that period restarts the 2h clock.
findings.evidence: risk.py:155-161: 'recent = list(self.recent)[-self.streak_n:]\n if (len(recent) >= self.streak_n and sum(1 for w in recent if not w) >= self.streak_losses and not self.killed):\n self.halt_until_us = _now_us() + int(self.cooloff_s * 1e6)' — no persistence of the original trip time; run.py:_seed_day_pnl feeds it all of today's outcomes.
findings.failure_scenario: Streak trips on variance at 10:00, cooloff ends 12:00, probe passes cleanly by 12:40, bot trading normally. A code deploy at 13:00 (restart_bots.sh restarts all coins) reruns seed(), still sees 6 losses in the day's last 20, and idles the bot until 15:00 — ~2h of forgone EV (~$50-140 for btc at the config note's own rate) on every post-halt-day deploy, across however many coins tripped.
findings.fix: Log the halt trip (and probe completion) as decision lines and have seed() honor the ORIGINAL halt_until timestamp (arming only the remaining time, zero if served); this pairs with the probe-kill persistence fix in the major finding.

findings.title: Re-run backfill_oracle on RTDS reconnect to repair integral holes
findings.claim: The recorder holds an independent RTDS connection and flushes every oracle tick for all five coins to data/live/rtds within ~50 ticks (recorder.py:134-138); backfill_oracle() already knows how to merge those files into oracle_hist de-duplicated by timestamp (state.py:427-465) but is only called once at startup. Calling it after each rtds_silent/feed_err reconnect would fill most outage holes with the real ticks the bot missed.
findings.evidence: run.py:330-337 reconnect handlers only log and sleep: 'except asyncio.TimeoutError:\n self.log_decision({"kind": "rtds_silent", ...})'; state.py:459-464 merge is idempotent: 'if ts in seen: continue ... self.oracle_hist.append((ts, px))' (note: appends must stay time-sorted — merge, then rebuild the deque sorted).
findings.failure_scenario: Concrete upside: it converts the held-price-hole exposure into a non-event whenever the bot's socket (not Chainlink itself) was the failure — the common case, since the recorder and bot fail independently — restoring accurate z within one 30s settle window instead of trading a contaminated integral, and shortening the post-restart blind window for K to seconds. At the config's own numbers (btc ~$648/day, edge concentrated in the settle window), each avoided contaminated/blind window is worth $1-5 of EV and avoids the ~$148 tail loss of a false 0.99-ask fire.
findings.fix: After each reconnect (and on rtds_round_stale), call self.state.backfill_oracle(lookback_s=120) and re-sort oracle_hist; skip if the recorder files are absent.

result.clean_areas: (1) Staleness gating structure: inputs_ok IS checked before every signal on both paths (event-driven _maybe_eval -> _try_market_inner run.py:764-778 and the 1s decide_loop), not just in the health line; oracle receipt-staleness (5s) plus round-age (20s in fair/zscore, 60s feed watchdog) is a sound layered design — the holes found are the specific ones reported (post-reconnect integral holes, settle-path coverage, book processing-time stamps). Binance death is correctly non-fatal by design (oracle fallback, guarded sigma with no-reference refusal, state.py:546-562 verified). CLOB full death stops trading via the 10s book gate; recv timeouts (10s/15s/30s) exist on all three sockets and the consumer-supervisor prevents the silent-consumer death mode. (2) Risk enforcement points all located and verified: per-market share/dollar caps at run.py:804-821 correctly include latency-queued orders (q_sh/q_usd) and both-sides blocking includes pending; max_concurrent counts pending slugs; settle_FAILED frees stuck slots after 1h. Day rollover is genuinely UTC (time.gmtime in risk.py:70,101; day_start in run.py:122 matches) — no timezone bug. day_pnl restart seeding works and the 32MB tail window is ample (decisions.jsonl measures ~450B/line; even a heavy coin-day is ~5-10MB, well inside 32MB). (3) Clock: chrony IS provisioned and enabled in droplet_setup.sh:20-29 with correct rationale; nothing else needed for the 2s-skew concern beyond (optionally) a chronyc waitsync before first bot start. (4) Deploy scripts: restart_bots.sh's restart-proof logic is correct including its set -e semantics; reset_pnl.sh stops units before archiving, its `is-active && stop` pattern does NOT trip set -e (guarded && list), and truncate-then-restart sequencing is safe; droplet_setup.sh's git hard-reset + config.local.json split, per-coin flock, and legacy-unit removal are sound. (5) Disk: not a launch risk on any realistic horizon — raw CLOB books are pruned hourly (keep-raw-hours 1), rtds/binance ticks have 7-day retention (~2.5-3GB steady state), logs/<coin>/*.jsonl grow only ~5-20MB/day total (health lines 2,880/day/coin at ~0.5-1.5KB plus bounded per-signal lines — signal volume is bounded because size_ok zeroes further signals once per-market caps are queued), and the bots write nothing to stdout so journald stays at its self-capped default; months to fill a 25GB droplet, though logs/<coin>/ has no rotation (slow leak, low consequence). (6) CLOB resubscribe cycle: subscribe-time full 'book' snapshots resync the level map within ~1-2s of each 240s rotation and mid-cycle market additions break out immediately (run.py:406-417); the residual gap exposure is covered in the book-timestamp finding. (7) Paper fill caps (participation/tape/lifetime-claimed) and the opposite-side/duplicate-book guards in strategy.py match their documented intent; consume() bookkeeping loss on restart is subsumed by the position-restore finding.

findings.title: No live order path exists at all; config's mode:'paper' key is dead code
findings.claim: There is zero py-clob-client (or any CLOB REST) integration anywhere in the repo, py-clob-client is not in requirements.txt, and the config key "mode": "paper" is never read by any code -- grep for cfg.get("mode") returns nothing -- so there is no mode switch to flip. The only reference to a live client is one sentence in bot/README.md:48. Everything below the strategy signal (order placement, auth, fills, positions, settlement cash) is simulation.
findings.evidence: bot/config.json:2: "mode": "paper",  -- never read anywhere. bot/run.py:7-9: "Live order mode is intentionally NOT implemented until paper-vs-backtest reconciliation passes". bot/README.md:48: "client (py-clob-client) with API creds wired into the PaperBroker interface". requirements.txt lists only pandas/numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/pyarrow/requests/python-dotenv/websockets/aiohttp -- no py-clob-client, no web3, no eth-account.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator who believes the launch is 'flip mode to live' ships nothing: editing config.json to "mode": "live" changes no behavior whatsoever, the bot keeps paper-trading, and the first real dollar is risked only after an entire client stack that does not exist yet is designed, built, and tested.
findings.fix: Build order: (1) read-only preflight script: run src/check_geoblock.py from the live host, fetch negRisk/orderMinSize/orderPriceMinTickSize per target market from Gamma/CLOB, verify chrony sync, read wallet balance+allowances; (2) key provisioning (see key-management finding); (3) LiveBroker: place FAK via py-clob-client (create_and_post_order, OrderArgs with correct neg_risk flag), parse response incl. 'delayed' status, authenticated user-channel websocket for fills, ack timeout, client-side order ids; (4) wire into run.py behind an explicit --live CLI flag AND config mode check (refuse to start if they disagree), sending at signal time and deleting the simulated latency/caps path in live mode; (5) reconciler + redemption worker; (6) stop-all script + alert webhook. Dry-run day 1: ONE coin, size=10 shares (venue min 5), max_market_shares=10, max_market_dollars=10, max_concurrent_markets=2, daily_loss_limit=25, other 4 coins stay paper; run 24h logging per-order ack latency, fill rate (expect ~65% reachability per venue_facts) and filled/requested ratio vs the paper model's prediction for the same order; scale 10 -> 50 -> 100 shares over a week only if live fill quality matches paper within ~20%.

findings.title: The promised 'single place to swap PaperBroker for a CLOB client' is not true
findings.claim: The execution logic does not live behind the broker interface. Bot._execute (run.py:818-918) walks the book, applies participation/tape/lifetime caps, samples a 1% reject, computes the fill legs itself, and only then calls broker.taker_fills() to RECORD the pre-decided fill; the simulated 410ms latency lives in Bot.pending (run.py:1030-1039, 86-87), not in the broker. PaperBroker.taker_fills is a ledger writer, not an order placer, so swapping the broker class cannot produce a live bot.
findings.evidence: run.py:8-9: "the execution interface is the single place to swap PaperBroker for a CLOB client." vs run.py:879: "want = min(budget, cap_book, cap_tape, cap_life)", run.py:913: "self.broker.taker_fills(o[\"slug\"], o[\"side\"], legs, meta=meta)", run.py:1034: "\"fire_us\": now_us() + self.latency_us" -- fill sizing, reject sampling and latency are all inside Bot, upstream of the broker.
findings.failure_scenario: A naive live build that swaps PaperBroker behind the same call sites inherits both paper artifacts: (a) orders sit in self.pending for venue_hold_ms+rtt_ms=410ms of SIMULATED delay before being sent, then suffer the venue's real 250ms hold on top -- ~660ms total, roughly doubling the adverse-selection window the edge was calibrated for (at the measured 0.5c/share/second decay, ~0.2c/share given away, ~10-20% of the +1-2c forward expectation); (b) the model-computed 'legs' get treated as the actual fill, so the position ledger diverges from the venue's reality on the very first partial.
findings.fix: Restructure before writing the client: extract an Executor interface at the SIGNAL boundary (submit(slug, token_id, side, limit, size) -> order_id) called directly from _try_market_inner's taker branch. PaperExecutor keeps the pending queue + fill model; LiveExecutor sends immediately and reports fills only from venue acks. Keep the paper model running in shadow on every live order (log what paper WOULD have filled) so live-vs-paper divergence is measurable per order from day one.

findings.title: No key management: bot never loads .env, units have no EnvironmentFile and run as root
findings.claim: Polymarket CLOB trading needs an L1 Polygon EOA private key (EIP-712 order signing) plus L2 API creds (key/secret/passphrase from create_or_derive_api_key). Nothing in the repo can hold or load either: python-dotenv is imported only by src/download_telonex.py (lines 15, 61-62); bot/run.py never touches os.environ or .env; the systemd units have no EnvironmentFile= and no User=, so a future key-bearing bot runs as root; and droplet_setup.sh documents the box hosting third-party code.
findings.evidence: droplet_setup.sh:127-132 [Service] block for jsf-paperbot@ contains only WorkingDirectory/ExecStart/Slice/Restart/RestartSec -- no User=, no EnvironmentFile=. droplet_setup.sh:57-58: "this droplet hosts processes that are not ours (/opt/polymarketstrat)". Only dotenv use in the codebase: src/download_telonex.py:61 "load_dotenv(...)" / 62 "key = os.environ[\"TELONEX_API_KEY\"]".
findings.failure_scenario: A hot wallet key placed on the current setup lives on a droplet running unknown third-party code (/opt/polymarketstrat) under root with no isolation; any compromise of the neighbour or the box drains the entire trading wallet -- an unbounded loss unrelated to the strategy. Five bot processes also share that one wallet and one L2 cred set with no coordination design.
findings.fix: Live host must be a DEDICATED droplet (Amsterdam per venue_facts tier analysis). Create a system user 'jsf'; keys in /opt/jsf/.env.live chmod 600 owned by jsf, loaded via EnvironmentFile=/opt/jsf/.env.live and User=jsf in a new jsf-livebot@.service; L1 key funds ONLY the day's trading bankroll (treat it as spendable); derive L2 creds once in the preflight script and cache them in the same file; never write any cred into config.json/config.local.json (config.local.json is shallow-merged into cfg and surfaces in logs). Verify .env.live matches a .gitignore pattern before the key ever exists.

findings.title: A real secret is already in pushed git history via committed audit transcripts
findings.claim: The .env file's TELONEX_API_KEY (tlx_REDACTED...) is committed in HEAD inside reports/audit_fleet_raw/agent-ab68b931b6858b2e7.jsonl (1 occurrence) and agent-ac275f21784fbd777.jsonl (3 occurrences), in commits pushed to origin (github.com/xin10ylop/JSF, branch claude/polymarket-btc-binaries-cy1f9p, in sync at b98e7d5). droplet_setup.sh clones that repo over unauthenticated https (line 15), so the repo is public and the key is exposed. .gitignore correctly excludes .env itself (line 1) -- the leak path is the audit fleet's auto-preserve loop committing raw agent transcripts that captured .env contents, bypassing .gitignore entirely.
findings.evidence: git grep tlx_REDACTED HEAD -> "HEAD:reports/audit_fleet_raw/agent-ab68b931b6858b2e7.jsonl:1" and "HEAD:reports/audit_fleet_raw/agent-ac275f21784fbd777.jsonl:3"; git branch -vv shows the branch in sync with origin; deploy/droplet_setup.sh:15: REPO_URL=https://github.com/xin10ylop/jsf.git cloned with no credentials; reports/audit_resume_state.md:88-90: "A background loop in the session pushes reports/audit_fleet_raw/ (fleet journal + every agent transcript, including partial in-flight work) every 4 minutes."
findings.failure_scenario: Today: anyone can use the Telonex key (paid data-quota theft; low direct dollar loss). At launch: the IDENTICAL mechanism -- session transcripts that captured key files, committed and pushed every 4 minutes -- captures the Polygon private key or L2 creds the moment any tooling reads .env.live, publishing a hot wallet key to a public GitHub repo; the wallet is drained in minutes.
findings.fix: Rotate the Telonex key now (it is burned regardless of history rewriting). Before any live key exists: stop committing raw agent transcripts, add reports/audit_fleet_raw/ to .gitignore or purge it from the branch, and adopt a hard rule that the live key file is never readable by anything that writes to the repo. Add a pre-push secret scan (gitleaks, or a grep for tlx_/0x[0-9a-f]{64} patterns) to the deploy flow.

findings.title: No funding layer: USDC balance, exchange allowances, negRisk routing all unhandled
findings.claim: Nothing in the repo touches USDC on Polygon, exchange allowances, or the negRisk flag. discover() reads only clobTokenIds from Gamma (run.py:251) and drops everything else, so the bot does not know whether a market routes to the standard CTF Exchange or the NegRisk exchange -- and an order signed for the wrong exchange contract is rejected. Grep for usdc/allowance/approve/negRisk across bot/ and src/ returns zero code hits. There is also no shared-balance concept: risk limits are per process, five processes spend one wallet.
findings.evidence: run.py:251: "toks = mk.get(\"clobTokenIds\")" -- the only field read from the market object besides the slug query. venue_facts.md:92-94 (quoting Polymarket docs): "if the market, balance, allowance, or risk checks fail when the delay expires, the order is rejected instead of matching." config.json:25 _per_process_note claims "$750 of concurrent market exposure" aggregate, but max_market_dollars=150 x max_concurrent_markets=4 x 5 coins = $3,000 worst case.
findings.failure_scenario: Live day 1: allowances never set -> every order fails the venue's re-validation at hold expiry and the bot books nothing while believing it should fill ~65% of sends. Or: wallet funded to the note's $750 figure while the caps actually permit $3,000 of concurrent open cost -> balance checks fail nondeterministically across five uncoordinated processes, producing a reject pattern n_reject cannot distinguish from venue flakiness.
findings.fix: Preflight (build stage 1-2): one-time approvals of USDC and CTF setApprovalForAll for the CTF Exchange AND NegRisk exchange/adapter contracts (py-clob-client documents the addresses), verified by reading allowances back. In discover(), also store the market's negRisk flag and tick size and pass them to order creation. Add a balance poll (every 30s) plus a pre-send reserve check against a shared ledger file: refuse to send if wallet_balance - open order cost < this order's cost. Fund day 1 with >= 3x the configured aggregate worst case at dry-run caps (trivial at $10/market), and correct the $750 note to $3,000 before anyone sizes a wallet off it.

findings.title: No way to learn a fill: no user channel, no order-response handling, no ack timeout
findings.claim: The only CLOB websocket is the public market channel (run.py:497: {"assets_ids": ids, "type": "market"}); there is no authenticated user-channel subscription, no order placement response parsing, no order-status polling, and no client order id. Live FAK on these markets returns 'delayed' at the 250ms hold, so the fill outcome does NOT come back synchronously -- the bot must consume its own trade/order events from the user channel or poll the order endpoint. Paper instead decides its own fill locally at fire time (run.py:900-913) and would have no source of truth for a real partial fill or a killed remainder.
findings.evidence: run.py:495-497: "async with websockets.connect(url, ...) as ws: await ws.send(json.dumps({\"assets_ids\": ids, \"type\": \"market\"}))" -- the only subscription in the codebase. venue_facts.md:90-97: "the order is held for 250 ms, then validation runs again and the order is matched or placed on the book" ... "Inside the window the order cannot be cancelled; resubmitting is rejected; dropping the connection does not stop it."
findings.failure_scenario: Bot POSTs a FAK for 100 shares; the HTTP response says 'delayed'; the connection then times out. The bot now has no idea whether it owns 0, 37, or 100 shares. If it assumes 0 and the z-signal persists, it re-fires and can end up 2x the per-market cap (the exact restart double-buy bug already fixed for paper, reintroduced live); if it assumes 100 and got 0, the settle ledger and daily loss limit run on fictional positions.
findings.fix: Build stage 3: authenticated user channel (L2 creds) consuming order/trade events keyed by order id; parse the placement response for immediate outcomes (matched/unmatched/delayed, taking/making amounts); treat an order as UNKNOWN until an ack, with a timeout of hold(250ms)+rtt+2s after which the bot polls the order endpoint before doing anything else in that market; count exposure as size REQUESTED (not filled) for all risk checks until the ack resolves -- the paper code's pending-queue exposure accounting (run.py:994-999) is the right pattern to carry over.

findings.title: Settlement cash assumed to reappear instantly; no redemption path, no gas plan
findings.claim: PaperBroker.settle() credits the $1.00 payoff the moment the bot's own oracle read decides the market (paper.py:126-127) and the capital is immediately reusable.
