Live, winning outcome tokens are ERC-1155 CTF positions that must be redeemed (redeemPositions on the CTF / negRisk adapter, or claimed via Polymarket's relayer/proxy wallet) before the USDC is spendable again, and self-redeeming from an EOA needs POL for gas. Nothing in the repo redeems, claims, or mentions this; venue_facts.md:27 notes venue settlement lands only ~20-60s after window end.
findings.evidence: paper.py:126-127: "payoff = pos[\"shares\"] * (1.0 if won else 0.0); pnl += payoff - pos[\"cost\"]" -- cash conjured at internal settle time. Grep for redeem/claim/gas/matic across bot/ returns nothing but doc comments (src/costs.py:7 "Winning shares redeem $1").
findings.failure_scenario: 5m markets settle every 5 minutes; at full caps a coin can lock $150-600 per cycle. If redemption is not automatic on this account's setup, buying power monotonically drains: with a $1,500 wallet and ~$300/coin-cycle across 5 coins, spendable USDC hits zero within the first hour while the paper-style P&L view says everything is fine -- every subsequent order dies at the hold's balance re-validation, and the edge (which lives on being present in the final 30-60s) silently stops harvesting.
findings.fix: Build stage 5: determine on the FIRST dry-run trade whether the operator's account setup (Polymarket proxy wallet vs raw EOA) auto-credits winnings; if not, add a redemption worker sweeping resolved condition ids every 1-2 minutes (batch redeemPositions; hold 5-10 POL -- redemptions cost cents on Polygon). Size day-1 bankroll at >= 10x configured concurrent exposure so a redemption stall degrades throughput, not correctness, and alert when spendable balance < 2x per-order cost.

findings.title: Position state is self-belief with no venue reconciliation, even on restart
findings.claim: broker.positions is built exclusively from the bot's own simulated fills, and the restart path (_replay_open_positions, run.py:113-162) replays the bot's OWN paper_fills.jsonl -- correct for paper, but live it re-derives belief from belief. There is no comparison against the venue's positions/balance (Polymarket data-api), no divergence alarm, and the per-market caps, the opposite-side guard (run.py:979-985) and the daily loss limit all run on this unverified ledger.
findings.evidence: run.py:113-114: "def _replay_open_positions(self): \"\"\"Rebuild positions in STILL-OPEN markets from the fills log.\"\"\"" -- the only position-recovery mechanism; no code anywhere queries a venue position or balance endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A live fill whose ack was lost (crash between POST and ack persistence) is absent from the log; after restart the bot sees zero shares in a market where it holds 100, buys the full cap again (the documented 2x-cap failure this function exists to prevent, resurrected by the paper-to-live gap), or buys the OPPOSITE side the guard would have blocked -- paying ~$1.90 for a $1.00 payoff, an instant ~47% loss on the doubled stake.
findings.fix: Build stage 5: on startup and every 60s, fetch positions and balance for the wallet from the data-api, diff against the local ledger, and on any mismatch: halt new orders for that market (or all, if balance diverges), log a reconcile_mismatch line, fire the alert webhook. Persist sent-order intents (order id, size, market) to disk BEFORE the POST so the restart path queries each unresolved order id instead of trusting the fill log.

findings.title: Kill switch gaps: no stop-all script, and the daily kill un-arms at UTC midnight
findings.claim: (1) No script or documented command stops all five processes instantly: restart_bots.sh:4-8 itself warns that `systemctl restart "jsf-paperbot@*"` "matches zero units and exits 0", RECOVERY.md never mentions stopping, and no deploy/stop_all.sh exists -- the operator must reconstruct five unit names under pressure. (2) The daily kill is not sticky: Risk._roll_day (risk.py:100-112) sets killed=False at UTC midnight, so a bot killed by the loss backstop or a confirmed-breakage probe kill resumes trading unattended hours later. (3) daily_loss_limit only blocks new orders and drops the pending queue (run.py:797-807) -- acceptable since positions self-expire in <=15min, but only if (2) is fixed, because 'killed' currently means 'paused until midnight'.

findings.title: Hybrid-z benchmark uses oracle ticks at round stamp; live arrival is 1-2.6s later
findings.claim: tape_chainlink (the source of the HYBRID-z ~+1.2c/sh, ~$694/day number that findings.md 9.8 sets as the forward launch expectation) indexes every Chainlink tick by its round timestamp and computes K, S and sigma at te = ts - lag from ticks stamped <= te. Live, those rounds reach the bot 1.0-2.6s after their stamps (I measured p5=1.01s, p50=1.56s, p95=2.21s, max=6.84s on the repo's own data/live/rtds capture, using the recorded t_local_us field this script ignores). So the oracle-legged tapes model a total decision lag of --lag=1s while the live bot's real oracle-leg information lag is ~1s (hold+rtt margin) PLUS ~1.6s delivery: the offline decider sees ~1.6s of settlement-series future relative to any real-time decider. tape_latency's claim that "lag=1 is ... about 2.5x the real 400 ms delay -- a conservative bound" (tape_latency.py:14-15) is only true for Binance-fed z, where the ws feed delivers in ~100ms; it is false for CHAINLINK-z and for the K/S/sigma legs of HYBRID-z.
findings.evidence: tape_chainlink.py:132 `out[int(p["timestamp"]) / 1000.0] = float(p["value"])`; :330 `S, cov, _ = ser.integral(t1 - w, te)`; :325 `sd1 = sig.loc[int(te)]`. Recorded tick shows the lag directly: {"payload":{..."timestamp":1786320304000,...},"t_local_us":1786320305784998} = 1.78s delivery. bot/state.py:70-72 already documents it: "Chainlink rounds arrive 1.6-2.8s after their round timestamps (measured p50/p99 on data/live/rtds)".
findings.failure_scenario: The project's own lag-decay table (findings.md 8.2: btc +2.13c at lag 0, +1.65 at 1s, +0.89 at 2s, +0.51 at 3s -- roughly -0.5 to -0.8c/sh per second) implies that moving the oracle legs from the modeled 1s to the reachable ~2.5s costs on the order of 0.3-0.8c/sh. Applied to a +1.2c/sh aggregate benchmark, the go/no-go number could be overstated by half or more; a launch sized to ~$700/day off this table may be sized to an unreachable figure. The 9.8 per-coin reconciliation (doge +5.18 vs live +4.73 etc.) is likewise flattered.
findings.fix: Rebuild the oracle Series keyed by t_local_us/1e6 (present in every rtds record) instead of payload.timestamp, keeping --lag for hold+rtt only; re-run tape_chainlink and re-derive the launch-bar row. Report both indexings side by side so the delivery-lag cost is measured, not assumed.

findings.title: Live z holds a stale price over the trailing settle-window gap vs fresh spot
findings.claim: zscore()/fair() build S = _integral(t1-w, now), and _integral holds the last RECEIVED oracle round's price all the way to now (state.py:646 `total += cur_px * (b_us - cur_t)`), while the future leg uses fresh basis-adjusted Binance spot (`r_sum + spot * rem - K * m.w`). The trailing 1-3s of already-elapsed window (delivery lag p50 1.56s plus inter-round spacing; passes the MAX_HOLE_S=5 guard) is therefore priced at a tick stamped up to ~2.6s ago, even though those un-arrived seconds are epistemically identical to the future seconds the model correctly extrapolates with spot. Settlement will record real Chainlink prices there, which track spot, not the stale tick. Quantified on the repo's own btc rtds capture: trailing gap p50 2.0s, p95 3.0s; the resulting z-numerator error at rem=10s is p95=0.29, p99=0.55, max=3.7 z-units unconditionally -- and sd shrinks like rem^1.5, so at rem=5s these scale x2.83 to p95~0.8, p99~1.6 against a firing gate of |z|>=2. The error is largest exactly during the fast moves that generate signals.
findings.evidence: state.py:843-848: `r_sum, _secs, _n, covered, hole = self._settle_full(m, t_us)` ... `return (r_sum + spot * rem - K * m.w) / sd`; state.py:643-646: `total += cur_px * (ts - cur_t)` / `total += cur_px * (b_us - cur_t)` where cur_px is the last received round's price; state.py:70-72 measured delivery lag 1.6-2.8s.
findings.failure_scenario: Price spikes down $15 over 3s then snaps back: the delivered rounds cover the dip, the trailing 2s of S is held at the dip price while spot has recovered; z_dn stays <= -2 after the true margin has faded, the bot buys a Down ask priced for the recovery and loses ~1.0/share when it settles Up. Symmetrically, in sustained moves S lags the move, |z| crosses the gate ~2s late and the bot pays an ask that has already repriced -- the project's own decay table prices each second of lag at ~0.5-0.8c/sh. Both directions lose relative to every offline tape, which has S complete to the decision instant.
findings.fix: In zscore() and fair(), integrate the oracle only to its last received tick t_last and extend with spot: numerator = S(t1-w -> t_last) + spot*(t1_s - t_last_s) - K*w (equivalently treat the undelivered elapsed seconds like the future leg). This also closes most of the live-vs-hybrid-tape information asymmetry in finding 1.

findings.title: Oracle-spot fallback fires on ~2s-stale spot at full rem weight, unmarked
findings.claim: When Binance is >3s stale, spot_adj() returns self.oracle_px -- the last received round, whose stamp is ~1.6-2.8s old in normal operation (up to ~5s inside the hole guard). zscore() multiplies that stale spot by the full remaining window (`spot * rem`, rem up to 30s for 5m and 60s for 15m), so the spot-leg error is rem times the price move over the staleness gap. Risk deliberately allows this regime: inputs_ok() dropped the Binance freshness requirement (risk.py:191-197 "Binance is an ENHANCEMENT, not a requirement") and gates only oracle receipt age <5s and book age. Nothing in the fired-signal record distinguishes fallback-spot fires from hybrid-spot fires (strategy.py stamps oracle_age_s but not binance age / spot source), yet the project's own tape says the pure-oracle-spot variant is materially worse: findings.md 9.7 CHAINLINK-z reads -0.88c (btc) and -0.24c (xrp) where the hybrid reads +0.78/+0.19 -- 'a lagged z fires worse'.
findings.evidence: state.py:781-785: `fresh = (self.binance_px is not None and (now_us() - self.binance_us) / 1e6 <= max_binance_age_s)` ... `return self.oracle_px`; risk.py:199-202: `return (not self.killed and not self.in_cooloff() and staleness["oracle_s"] < self.stale_oracle_s and book_age_s < self.stale_book_s)` -- no binance term; state.py:773-775 documents the throttled mirror ("~2.6 trades/s with 2 distinct prices per 20s from this host") that makes the fallback regime routine.
findings.failure_scenario: Binance ws goes quiet for 10s (the observed throttling/silent-socket regime) during a $10, 3-sigma move; spot = the pre-move oracle round. At rem=20s the z numerator is off by 20 x $10 = $200 against sd ~ $117 (sigma $2.28/sqrt(s) measured on the capture) -- a ~1.7 z-unit error at full gate size, either firing on a signal that no longer exists or into the wrong side of a 15m market. Live money is lost in a regime no offline tape validated, and post-hoc analysis cannot even isolate those fills.
findings.fix: Log spot source (hybrid vs oracle-fallback) and binance_age_s on every fired signal; then either refuse RollAvgEdge fires on fallback spot for the coins where the CHAINLINK-z tape is <= 0 (btc, xrp), or shrink the gate (raise zmin) in that regime until paper data shows the fallback fires pay.

findings.title: oracle_vs_binance drops calm near-tie markets where the series disagree most
findings.claim: Three survivorship/weighting choices all bias the measured Binance-vs-Chainlink disagreement DOWN: (a) mean_from requires >=50% per-second tick coverage of each window, and oracle tick density is activity-driven (the feed misses ~38% of seconds, state.py:523), so calm windows -- exactly the small-margin markets where sign disagreements concentrate -- are preferentially excluded; (b) the oracle mean is an unweighted tick mean rather than the time-weighted integral the bot and the venue use, over-weighting burst seconds; (c) outcomes() silently drops voided/unresolved markets (`if not op: continue`) and whole 100-slug chunks on any HTTP error -- near-ties again. The 9.6 disagree% table (0.7-5.1%) built on this is still quoted as the size of the proxy handicap.
findings.evidence: oracle_vs_binance.py:132-135: `vals = [series[s] for s in range(int(a), int(b)) if s in series]` / `if len(vals) < (b - a) / 2: return None`; :86-97: `if not op: continue` and `except Exception: continue` inside outcomes(); state.py:522-523: "the feed misses ~38% of seconds".
findings.failure_scenario: The measured 0.7-5.1% mis-sign rates understate the true proxy error on the full market population; any future sizing that reuses the 9.6 drag arithmetic (already once used to 'explain' the live-vs-tape gap to within 0.02c before 9.7 refuted it) inherits a too-small handicap and over-credits Binance-based tapes.
findings.fix: Use a held-price time-weighted integral (mirror BotState._integral with the same MAX_HOLE guard) instead of the tick mean, report the count and margin distribution of markets excluded for coverage, and count voided/failed-fetch markets explicitly rather than dropping them.

findings.title: tape_capacity uses lag-0 z, flattering bucket economics behind min_price gates

Polymarket says "eu-west-2", never "AWS". `eu-west-2` is AWS's region code for London, and third parties assert it directly — Glassnode's latency monitor describes its target as *"REST round-trip to Polymarket (clob.polymarket.com, origin AWS eu-west-2 London)"*. I could not independently confirm AWS: `clob.polymarket.com` resolves only to Cloudflare anycast (`2606:4700:440d::6812:22cd`, `2606:4700:4408::ac40:9933`), so the origin is masked.

**Two things worth flagging:**

- **Polymarket's own recommendation is eu-west-1 (Dublin), not Amsterdam.** "Closest Non-Georestricted Region: eu-west-1" is Polymarket telling builders where to sit. Among AWS regions that's correct — eu-west-3 Paris (FR) and eu-central-1 Frankfurt (DE) are tier-2 blocked, eu-south-1 Milan (IT) is tier-2. Amsterdam is not an AWS region, which is why it never appears in that framing.
- **Tension you should raise with support:** eu-west-2 is London = GB, itself a **tier-2 close-only-on-API** jurisdiction. Yet Polymarket sells co-location there. Co-located customers are presumably whitelisted, but that is nowhere documented. Do not build around it without written confirmation.

**Latency.** No official Polymarket figures exist. Glassnode's prediction-market monitor is purpose-built for this (probes in Amsterdam, Dublin, London, Frankfurt; refresh every 5s) but currently returns *"No data yet. Waiting for probe rollups…"* — so there is no public measured dataset today.

Unofficial, physics/typical-network floors (my characterization, **not** sourced from Polymarket):
| Path | Distance | Typical RTT |
|---|---|---|
| in-region eu-west-2 | — | <1–2 ms |
| **Amsterdam ↔ London** | ~360–400 km | **~7–10 ms** |
| **Dublin ↔ London** | ~465 km subsea | **~10–12 ms** |

**Amsterdam is normally *faster* to London than Dublin is** — which inverts the affiliate-blog advice. quantvps/newyorkcityservers claim *"Traders in Dublin enjoy an advantage with latencies of just 0–1ms"*; that is impossible, since the speed of light in fiber alone puts a ~4.6 ms RTT floor on Dublin–London. Disregard those numbers.

Important architectural caveat: because the CLOB sits behind Cloudflare anycast, your RTT is to the nearest Cloudflare edge (AMS or LHR) **plus** Cloudflare→origin — not a direct path to eu-west-2. That is exactly what the co-location offer exists to bypass, and it means shaving 2–3 ms of AMS-vs-DUB backbone difference is largely noise against the Cloudflare hop.

---

## 5. RTDS — Chainlink price stream socket

**Verdict: open, unauthenticated, no geo restriction, no documented connection limit. Empirically confirmed.**

Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/market-data/chainlink-twap

Endpoint: `wss://ws-live-data.polymarket.com`

> "RTDS is the recommended production integration. It relays Chainlink-computed mainnet TWAP updates **without credentials**."

> "RTDS uses an application-level heartbeat. Send the text frame `PING` every 5 seconds to maintain the connection."

> "Subscriptions start with the next update. There is no snapshot, history, or replay after a disconnect." … "Direct clients must reconnect and resubscribe after a disconnect."

**I verified this live.** I connected with no auth *from the US datacenter IP that is geoblocked for order placement*, subscribed, and received live ticks — doge/usd, sol/usd, bnb/usd, zec/usd, eth/usd. So RTDS is definitively **not** geo-gated and **not** credentialed. The server assigns a `connection_id` per socket.

Practical details:
- Topics: `crypto_prices_twap_thirty` (30s), `crypto_prices_twap_sixty` (60s); also `crypto_prices`, `crypto_prices_chainlink`.
- `filters` must be exact compact JSON, lowercase, no spaces: `{"symbol":"btc/usd"}`. Omit for all symbols. Verbatim: *"If you need several symbols for one window, omit `filters` and filter updates by `payload.symbol` in your application."*
- **Use `full_accuracy_value`** (signed E18 fixed-point string), divide by 10^18. The numeric `value` is *"provided only for display convenience"* — do not trade off it.
- `payload.timestamp` = Chainlink observation time; outer `timestamp` = RTDS publish time. Use the former for freshness.
- 30s/60s are **lookback windows, not publication cadences.** Docs warn: do not infer the window from update frequency, and do not attempt to reproduce the TWAP yourself — *"Chainlink does not currently publish the custom feed's sampling boundaries, weighting, rounding, or missing-input behavior."*

**Connection limits: none documented, anywhere.** I grepped `rate-limits.md`, `trading-rate-limits.md`, `realtime-data.md` and `wss/market.md` — zero hits for connection/concurrency caps. The Cloudflare IP limits page covers REST only. Treat this as *undocumented*, not *unlimited*. The docs nudge toward a single socket: *"The Real-Time Data Service (RTDS) carries reference prices and comments over a shared real-time connection. Subscribe only to the topics your application needs."*

⚠️ Heartbeat mismatch to watch: RTDS wants `PING` every **5s**; the CLOB market channel (`wss/market.md`) wants *"Send PING every 10 seconds"*. Different services, different intervals.

---

## 6. Does Cloudflare block datacenter IPs (DO AMS3) on the CLOB specifically?

**Verdict: no blanket datacenter block — confirmed by direct test. But intermittent Cloudflare bot-management 403s on automated order POSTs are real, community-reported, and unresolved by Polymarket.**

Evidence against a blanket block: from an Anthropic datacenter IP I got `200` on `GET /ok` and `GET /sampling-simplified-markets`, and the `POST /order` rejection was an explicit **geo** message, not a bot challenge. Datacenter origin per se is not the discriminator.

Confirmed Cloudflare presence on the CLOB: `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray: …-IAD`, `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`, and a `__cf_bm` cookie — `__cf_bm` is specifically **Cloudflare Bot Management**.

Official, on rate limiting: *"The limits on this page are IP-based and enforced using Cloudflare's throttling system. When you exceed the limit for any endpoint, requests are throttled (delayed/queued) rather than immediately rejected."* — https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/rate-limits. Relevant caps: `POST /order` 5,000 req/10s burst, 120,000 req/10min sustained.

**Community-reported only (NOT official, no Polymarket response):**
- `Polymarket/py-clob-client` **#143 "Create Order Cloudflare Blocks"** (opened 2025-07-30): Cloudflare blocks hit `create_order()`/`post_order()` while other calls succeed. Reporter tried residential proxies across multiple geographies and Playwright, none worked. Quote: *"the whole point of the library is to develop bots, yet they have setup Cloudflare to block that exact behaviour."* No staff reply; still open.
- `py-clob-client` #91 (403 on API-key creation), `poly-market-maker` #72, plus a Cloudflare community thread reporting **30–50% intermittent** WAF blocks on server-to-server POSTs to the CLOB.

**No official documentation of datacenter/ASN blocking exists, and nothing anywhere names DigitalOcean or AMS3.** I have no evidence either way for AMS3 specifically — you'd need to test from the droplet itself.

⚠️ **Toolchain flag:** `Polymarket/py-clob-client` was **archived 2026-05-25**. The current first-party clients are `@polymarket/client` (TS, ≥0.3.0, Node 24+) and `polymarket-client` (Python, ≥0.3.0, Py 3.11+). If your bot is on py-clob-client you are on dead code, and some of those Cloudflare reports may reflect stale request signing.

---

## Bottom line for the Amsterdam droplet

The narrow technical claim holds: per the developer docs, NL is tier-3 and the CLOB should accept orders from a Dutch IP. Everything around that claim is shaky:

1. Polymarket's Help Center says the opposite about NL, so the "API is open" line has no policy weight.
2. The KSA order is live, upheld on appeal, and already forced NL IP-blocking once in Feb 2026 — the gap is a lagging inconsistency under active regulatory pressure, closable overnight.
3. The ToS attestation covers being *located in* a restricted jurisdiction, not just VPN use, and the enforcement remedy is close-only mode on your wallet — which strands open positions rather than just stopping new ones.
4. Polymarket's own steer is **eu-west-1 (Dublin)**, and Dublin sits in the same tier-3 ambiguity as NL anyway — so it buys you consistency with Polymarket's documented recommendation, but not legal safety.

The latency argument does not rescue Amsterdam either: AMS's ~2–3 ms edge over Dublin is swamped by the Cloudflare anycast hop, and the only path that actually wins on latency — co-location in eu-west-2 — routes through the KYC/KYB form, which is exactly where an NL-resident operator's residence documentation becomes the blocking issue.

If low latency to the matching engine is the real goal, the KYC/KYB co-location form is the only officially supported answer, and it's worth asking Polymarket support two questions in writing before you build: (a) what jurisdiction they require for a co-located API trader given eu-west-2 is itself GB, and (b) whether the tier-3 NL/IE API carve-out in the developer docs is intentional policy or a documentation error. Their answer to (b) determines whether this project has a foundation at all.

**Unverified items, flagged honestly:** full ToS body text and the existence/wording of "Section 2.1.4" (client-rendered, not retrievable); measured AMS/DUB/LON latency to the CLOB (no public dataset exists); AWS as the eu-west-2 provider (origin masked by Cloudflare); and whether DO AMS3 ranges specifically are treated differently (untestable from here).

**Verified 2026-08-12 (all live checks run today). Sources: docs.polymarket.com, help.polymarket.com, status.polymarket.com, plus live Gamma/CLOB API reads.**

---

**1) 250 ms taker hold, non-cancellable during the hold — TRUE** (with one wording correction)

`https://docs.polymarket.com/concepts/order-lifecycle` (live today), exact quotes:
> "**Taker delay:** used on selected crypto and finance up/down markets. The order is held for 250 ms, then validation runs again and the order is matched or placed on the book. The API waits for this hold and returns the final order result. To check a specific market, call the public CLOB endpoint `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/clob-markets/{condition_id}` and look for `itode: true`."
> "During either delay, the order is pending and cannot be canceled. If the market, balance, allowance, or risk checks fail when the delay expires, the order is rejected instead of matching."
> "You can cancel orders at any time before they're matched via the CLOB API, **except while a marketable order is in a pending delay window**."

Live confirmation — `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/clob-markets/{condition_id}` returns `itode: true` for 5m (`btc-updown-5m-*`, `eth-updown-5m-*`), 15m (`eth-updown-15m-*`) **and hourly** (`hype-up-or-down-august-14-2026-6pm-et`) crypto up/down markets.

Correction: "reintroduced ~2026-06-05" is imprecise. The 250 ms delay already existed; the **Jun 5, 2026** change was making it *non-cancellable*. Announced only on X (@PolymarketDevs, `https://x.com/x/status/2061930696323830158`, ~Jun 3 2026): "On Friday Jun 5, we're changing how taker orders behave during the 250ms taker delay on these markets. Once your order clears initial validation and enters the delay window, it's locked in as pending until…" **This is not in the official changelog** — `https://docs.polymarket.com/changelog/predictions` has no June 5 entry. Doc page carries no date/version stamp.

---

**2) Taker fee 0.07·p·(1−p) per share, makers pay 0, ~20% maker rebate — TRUE, but incomplete**

`https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees` (live today):
> "`fee = C × feeRate × p × (1 - p)`" … "Where **C** = number of shares traded and **p** = price of the shares."
> "**Makers are never charged fees.** Only takers pay fees."
> Table: `| Crypto | 0.07 | 0 | 20% |` (Taker Fee Rate / Maker Fee Rate / Maker Rebate)
> Crypto fee table: $0.50 → $1.75 per 100 shares; $0.99 → $0.07 per 100 shares.

`https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/maker-rebates`: `| Crypto | 20% | Fee-curve weighted |`, paid daily in pUSD, $1 minimum payout.

Live per-market confirmation (Gamma, `btc-updown-5m-1786658100`): `feeSchedule = {'exponent': 1, 'rate': 0.07, 'takerOnly': True, 'rebateRate': 0.2}`, `feeType = crypto_fees_v2`. CLOB `fd = {'r': 0.07, 'e': 1, 'to': True}`.

**MISSING FROM THE BOT'S MODEL — `https://docs.polymarket.com/programs/taker-rebates` (live May 28, 2026):** takers now get a 30-day-volume tiered rebate on fees paid: Bronze $2k wV → 3%, Silver $20k → 8%, Gold $200k → 18%, Platinum $1M → 32%, Diamond $4M → 44%, Obsidian $10M+ → 50%. Crypto has the highest category weight (**2.3**) and `wV = Trade Size × (1 − Entry Price) × Category Weight × Bonuses`. Note buying at 0.99 earns almost no wV (upside 0.01). So 0.07·p·(1−p) is the *gross* worst case; net taker cost can be up to 50% lower.

Minor inconsistency: `help.polymarket.com/en/articles/13364471-maker-rebates-program` (updated Jul 21, 2026) lists Sports at 20%; docs and the Jul 10 changelog say 15%. Crypto = 20% in both.

---

**3) orderMinSize = 5, tick = 0.01 — TRUE. Tick → 0.001 above 0.96 / below 0.04 — CHANGED (not in effect; do not rely on it)**

Live reads on current 5m/15m/hourly/4h crypto up/down markets: Gamma `orderMinSize = 5`, `orderPriceMinTickSize = 0.01`; CLOB `clob-markets` `mos: 5`, `mts: 0.01`; `GET /tick-size?token_id=…` → `{"minimum_tick_size":0.01}`. `https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/place-orders` shows `"min_order_size": "5", "tick_size": "0.01"` and "the share quantity is above the minimum of `5`".

**The 0.96/0.04 dynamic-tick rule could not be reproduced and is contradicted by live data.** I scanned 400 open markets and probed the boundary cases directly:
- `highest-temperature-in-paris-on-august-13-2026-39c`, outcome prices `["0.035","0.965"]`, configured tick 0.01 → `GET /tick-size` returns **0.01** for both tokens, and the live book grid is `asks ['0.99','0.98','0.97']`, `bids [… '0.94','0.95']` — pure 0.01 increments, no 0.001 levels.
- `lowest-temperature-in-seoul-on-august-13-2026-23c` at `0.985`/`0.015`, configured tick 0.01 → `/tick-size` = **0.01**.
- Every 0.001-tick market sampled (prices 0.0005 → 0.9995) had CLOB `mts = 0.001` *configured*; `mts` always equalled the effective tick. In CLOB V2 tick size reads as a static per-market config, not price-dependent.

Practical consequence for your bot: with tick 0.01 the price grid is 0.01–0.99, so **buying asks up to 0.99 is valid and there is no 0.001 grid to handle** on these markets. The mechanism does still exist — `https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/wss/market` documents a `tick_size_change` event with `old_tick_size`/`new_tick_size`, described only as "Market tick size update when price approaches limits", with **no thresholds published**. Docs advise: "If your integration stores `tick_size` for later orders, listen for the `tick_size_change` event … The CLOB rejects an order whose price does not conform to the market's current tick size." Subscribe to it rather than hardcoding either value.

Also relevant and possibly not in your model: GTD orders — "GTD orders expire one minute before their stated expiration as a security threshold… the expiration must be at least **3 minutes** in the future — orders expiring sooner are rejected — so the minimum effective lifetime is about two minutes." That is longer than a 5m market's life, so GTD is largely unusable there. Liquidity-reward params on 5m markets: `r = {'mi': 50, 'ma': 4.5, 'moas': 30}` (min size 50, max spread 4.5¢, min order age 30s).

---

**4) TWAP settlement rule — PARTIALLY TRUE; two material corrections; no change announced after 2026-08-07**

Confirmed: effective **Aug 7, 2026 00:00 UTC**, crypto up/down markets resolve off Chainlink TWAP streams. Live market description (Gamma, `btc-updown-5m-1786658100`), verbatim:
> "This market will resolve to "Up" if the time-weighted average price (TWAP) of Bitcoin, generated by Chainlink, of the time range specified in the title is greater than or equal to **the price at the beginning of that range**. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Down".
> The resolution source for this market is information from Chainlink, specifically the BTC/USD TWAP data stream available at https://data.chain.link/streams/btc-usd-twap-30s-streams.
> Please note that this market is about the price according to the TWAP Chainlink data stream for the asset pair BTC/USD, not according to any other sources or spot markets."

`cryptoMarketConfig = {'id': 'btc-5m-twap-30', 'asset': 'btc', 'duration': '5m', 'twapEnabled': True, 'twapLookbackSeconds': 30}`. `https://docs.polymarket.com/market-data/chainlink-twap` confirms trailing semantics: "The 30-second and 60-second values are **lookback windows**, not publication cadences."

**Correction A — the slug is per-asset, not a single `twap-30s-streams`:** `btc-usd-twap-30s-streams`, `eth-usd-twap-30s-streams`, `sol-usd-…`, `xrp-usd-…`, `doge-usd-…`, `bnb-usd-…`, `hype-usd-…`, `zec-usd-…`.

**Correction B — "30s for 5m" is NOT universal. ZEC 5m markets use a 60s window:** live `zec-updown-5m-*` has `cryptoMarketConfig = {'id': 'zec-5m-twap-60', 'asset': 'zec', 'duration': '5m', 'twapEnabled': True, 'twapLookbackSeconds': 60}` and `resolutionSource = https://data.chain.link/streams/zec-usd-twap-60s-streams`. Read `cryptoMarketConfig.twapLookbackSeconds` per market; do not infer it from duration.

**CANNOT-VERIFY — "evaluated at BOTH the open and close boundaries."** No official source states the open value is itself a TWAP. The rule text says only "the price at the beginning of that range." Since the market declares the TWAP stream as its *sole* price source ("not according to any other sources or spot markets"), the open value is almost certainly the same stream sampled at the open timestamp — i.e. a trailing TWAP — but Polymarket has not written that down. The description is internally ambiguous besides: "TWAP … **of the time range specified in the title**" reads as an average over the whole 5 minutes, which contradicts `twapLookbackSeconds: 30`. Treat the open-boundary semantics as an unconfirmed assumption and validate empirically against resolved markets before sizing on it. Chainlink adds: "Chainlink does not currently publish the custom feed's sampling boundaries, weighting, rounding, or missing-input behavior, so do not independently reproduce the value without a specification from Chainlink."

**No rule change announced after 2026-08-07.** `https://docs.polymarket.com/changelog/predictions` latest entry is **Aug 10, 2026** and is Data-API-only (per-outcome redemptions, `grossInitialValue`/`entryFeesUsdc`, `includeArchived`, artwork fallback). Note the Aug 7 TWAP change itself never appeared in the official changelog — it was announced via X (@PolymarketDevs, ~Jul 30 2026) and covered by CoinDesk (Aug 7, 2026, `https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/07/how-a-five-second-trick-let-traders-drain-millions-from-polymarket`). **The changelog is not a reliable monitor for crypto-binary rule changes.**

---

**5) Families and coins — CHANGED (three coins you don't have; two families don't use TWAP)**

Live series enumeration (Gamma `/series`, all `active: true, closed: false`):

| Family | Recurrence | Coins | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5m | `5m` | btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, **bnb**, **hype**, **zec** | Chainlink TWAP 30s (**zec: 60s**) |
| 15m | `15m` | btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, **bnb**, **hype**, **zec** | Chainlink TWAP 60s |
| 4h | `daily` | btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, **bnb**, **hype**, **zec** | Chainlink TWAP 60s |
| hourly | `hourly` | btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, bnb, hype (**no zec**) | **Binance 1H candle open/close — NOT TWAP** |
| daily | `daily` | btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, bnb, hype (**no zec**) | **Binance 1-minute candle closes, noon ET — NOT TWAP** |

**BNB, HYPE and ZEC are live and absent from your list.** Press coverage (cryptobriefing / coinpaprika, Jul 30–Aug 7 2026) names only seven assets under the TWAP rules — BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, HYPE, BNB, DOGE — so **ZEC appears to be a post-announcement addition**, which is consistent with it being the one asset with a non-standard 60s window on 5m.

Series slugs are inconsistent between families: `btc-up-or-down-5m` / `btc-up-or-down-15m` / `btc-up-or-down-4h` but `bitcoin-up-or-down-hourly` / `solana-up-or-down-daily` / `dogecoin-up-or-down-daily`. Don't construct slugs by template.

Hourly resolution text, verbatim: "This market will resolve to "Up" if the close price is greater than or equal to the open price for the BTC/USDT 1 hour candle that begins on the time and date specified in the title." HYPE hourly uses Binance **futures** (`https://www.binance.com/en/futures/HYPEUSDT`), the rest use spot. If your bot treats all up/down families as TWAP-settled, hourly and daily are mispriced.

---

**6) CLOB rate limits — CHANGED (a new per-signer limiter went live in warning mode Jul 24, 2026)**

Two independent layers now. `https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/trading-rate-limits` (per-signer token buckets, order and cancel buckets separate):

> "Beginning **July 24, 2026**, the limiter will run in warning mode for two weeks. Requests will continue to be processed during this period. A request that would be rejected after live enforcement begins will include `Poly-RateLimit-Warning: true`… Polymarket will announce when live enforcement begins."

| Tier | 30-Day Volume | Order rate/s | Order burst | Cancel rate/s | Cancel burst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | — | 40 | 60 | 80 | 120 |
| Copper | $30k+ | 60 | 90 | 120 | 180 |
| Bronze | $50k+ | 80 | 120 | 160 | 240 |
| Silver | $100k+ | 200 | 300 | 400 | 600 |
| Gold | $500k+ | 400 | 600 | 800 | 1,200 |
| Platinum | $2.5M+ | 450 | 675 | 900 | 1,350 |
| Diamond | $5M+ | 525 | 787 | 1,050 | 1,575 |
| Elite | $10M+ | 600 | 900 | 1,200 | 1,800 |

Token costs: `POST /order` = 1; `POST /orders` = number of orders; `DELETE /order` = 1; `DELETE /orders` = number of IDs; `DELETE /cancel-all` and `/cancel-market-orders` = "1 plus the number of orders canceled". "a batch is admitted only when the bucket contains enough tokens for every entry. Otherwise, the entire request is rejected and no entries are processed." Tier assignments "refresh every three hours". Headers: `Poly-RateLimit-Remaining`, `-Reset`, `-Tier`, `Retry-After` on 429.

Two warnings for a 5m bot: a **new-signer address starts at Standard = 40 orders/s, burst 60**, and `Poly-RateLimit-Remaining` "can be negative after `DELETE /cancel-all`", blocking subsequent cancels until the bucket recovers. Since taker orders on these markets cannot be cancelled during the 250 ms hold, a cancel-storm plus a debt-ed cancel bucket is a live failure mode.

`https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/rate-limits` (Cloudflare IP-based, "throttled (delayed/queued) rather than immediately rejected", sliding windows, "remain unchanged"): CLOB general 9,000/10s; `/book` 1,500/10s; `/books` 500/10s; `/price` 1,500/10s; `/prices` 500/10s; `/midpoint` 1,500/10s; `/midpoints` 500/10s; `/prices-history` 1,000/10s; **market tick size 200/10s**; `/trades`,`/orders`,`/notifications`,`/order` 900/10s; `GET` balance allowance 200/10s. Gamma: general 4,000/10s, `/markets` 300/10s, `/events` 500/10s, combined listing 900/10s. Data API: general 1,000/10s, `/trades` 200/10s, `/positions` 150/10s. The 200/10s tick-size cap matters if you poll tick size per market per cycle across 8 coins × 3 families.

---

**7) July–August 2026 changes — several, none suspending crypto binaries; one breaking API change already shipped**

From `https://docs.polymarket.com/changelog/predictions`:
- **Jul 2, 2026** — "All World Cup *to advance*, *moneyline*, *spreads*, and *totals* markets are now decimalized to a **0.0025 (0.25¢)** tick size." (not crypto)
- **Jul 10, 2026** — "The sports taker fee rate increases from `0.03` to `0.05`" at midnight UTC; sports maker rebate 25% → 15%. **Crypto rate unchanged at 0.07.**
- **Jul 14, 2026** — CLOB v1 Neg Risk Adapter retired; relayer redeems to the old adapter available until Jul 17, 2026 00:00 UTC.
- **Jul 17, 2026 (rollout Jul 24, 04:00 UTC) — BREAKING:** "`POST /order` and `POST /orders` will no longer return `transactionHashes` on successful FAK/FOK matches — you get `tradeIDs` instead." Poll trades by `tradeID` until each has a hash or returns `FAILED`. **If your bot reads `transactionHashes` off FOK/FAK responses, it is already broken.**
- **Jul 24, 2026** — per-signer rate limiter in warning mode (item 6).
- **Aug 7, 2026 00:00 UTC** — TWAP settlement (item 4). Not in the changelog; X + CoinDesk only.
- **Aug 10, 2026** — Data API: per-outcome redemptions, `grossInitialValue` and `entryFeesUsdc` position fields, `includeArchived` on `GET /positions`.
- Also in force: **$1,000,000 in August liquidity rewards** across affected crypto up/down markets (announced with the TWAP change).

From `https://status.polymarket.com/default/history/1`:
- **Aug 13, 2026** — scheduled CLOB maintenance **04:30–05:00 UTC**; "Users might receive HTTP 503 errors during order placement/cancellation." *This is tomorrow — pause the bot for that window.*
- Aug 12 — Trading partial outage, order submission failures (resolved). Jul 30 — degraded trading performance / slowed order processing (~35 min). Jul 28–29 — `/price-history` lag, trading maintenance with rollback. Aug 10/11/12 — perps incidents (not predictions).

**No crypto fee change, no crypto market suspensions, and no crypto tick/min-size change in July–August 2026.**

---

## Headline: the API you asked about has been replaced

**`py-clob-client` is archived and non-functional.** The repo banner reads: *"This repository has been archived and is no longer maintained. The client is no longer functional and should not be used for new or existing integrations."* → migrate to `polymarket-client` (repo `Polymarket/py-sdk`), **v0.5.0, published 2026-08-07, requires Python ≥3.11**.

The reason it's dead is structural, not cosmetic — Polymarket shipped **CTF Exchange V2** (audited March 2026) plus a new collateral token and a new wallet type. `py_clob_client/config.py` still hardcodes the V1 exchange `0x4bFb41d5…` and USDC.e `0x2791Bca1…`; both are superseded. Everything below reflects V2 as live today.

| | V1 (py-clob-client) | V2 (current) |
|---|---|---|
| Exchange | `0x4bFb41d5B3570DeFd03C39a9A4D8dE6Bd8B8982E` | `0xE111180000d2663C0091e4f400237545B87B996B` |
| NegRisk exchange | `0xC5d563A36AE78145C45a50134d48A1215220f80a` | `0xe2222d279d744050d28e00520010520000310F59` |
| Collateral | USDC.e `0x2791Bca1…` | **pUSD** `0xC011a7E12a19f7B1f670d46F03B03f3342E82DFB` |
| EIP-712 domain version | `"1"` | `"2"` |
| Signed struct | had `nonce`, `feeRateBps`, `expiration`, `taker` | those are **gone**; added `signatureType`, `timestamp`, `metadata`, `builder` |
| Signature types | 0/1/2 | 0/1/2 **+ 3 (Deposit Wallet)** |

Install: `pip install polymarket-client` (imports as `polymarket`).

---

## 1. Auth — L1 vs L2

Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/getting-started/api (§Authentication), https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/wallets-auth

| Layer | Mechanism | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **L1** | Wallet signs EIP-712 `ClobAuth` | Create/derive API credentials **only** |
| **L2** | HMAC-SHA256 with API secret | Every private CLOB request |

L1 typed data — domain `{name:"ClobAuthDomain", version:"1", chainId:137}` (no `verifyingContract`), type `ClobAuth(address address,string timestamp,uint256 nonce,string message)`, message string exactly `"This message attests that I control the given wallet"`.

Exchange it at:
- `POST https://clob.polymarket.com/auth/api-key` (create)
- `GET  https://clob.polymarket.com/auth/derive-api-key` (idempotent re-derive — **use this on restart**, create will collide)

Both take headers `POLY_ADDRESS`, `POLY_SIGNATURE`, `POLY_TIMESTAMP`, `POLY_NONCE`. Response: `{apiKey, secret, passphrase}`. The credentials are deterministic per `(signer, nonce)` — nonce `0` unless you want multiple key sets.

L2 signing:
```
message = timestamp + METHOD + request_path [+ exact serialized body]
sig     = urlsafe_b64_with_padding(HMAC_SHA256(b64decode(secret), message))
```
Query params are **not** part of the signed path. Headers on every private call: `POLY_ADDRESS`, `POLY_SIGNATURE`, `POLY_TIMESTAMP`, `POLY_API_KEY`, `POLY_PASSPHRASE`.

**Order placement needs both**: L2 authenticates the HTTP request; a separate EIP-712 wallet signature authorizes the order payload itself.

---

## 2. Signature types and the funder address

From the installed SDK, `polymarket/_internal/wallet.py` — this is authoritative and **contradicts the OpenAPI spec**, which still lists only 0/1/2:

```python
_SIGNATURE_TYPE_BY_WALLET = {"EOA": 0, "POLY_PROXY": 1, "GNOSIS_SAFE": 2, "DEPOSIT_WALLET": 3}
```

Note type 2 is **Gnosis Safe** (legacy MetaMask/Rabby accounts), not "browser wallet proxy" generically; type 1 is the legacy Magic/Google email proxy. Both are legacy — per the docs, *"All Polymarket account wallets deployed on or after May 4, 2026"* are **Deposit Wallets**.

**For a fresh programmatic wallet: signature type 3, funder = the derived Deposit Wallet address, signer = your EOA.** They are different addresses. The Deposit Wallet is CREATE2-derived from the signer:

```
factory = 0x00000000000Fb5C9ADea0298D729A0CB3823Cc07
beacon  = 0x7A18EDfe055488A3128f01F563e5B479D92ffc3a
walletId = bytes32(signer);  args = abi.encode(factory, walletId);  salt = keccak256(args)
depositWallet = CREATE2(factory, salt, initCodeHashERC1967BeaconProxy(beacon, args))
```
The SDK does this for you — `classify_wallet_type()` derives all four candidates and matches. You pass `private_key` + `wallet`; it infers the type and signature type. Pass `wallet == signer_address` to get EOA/type 0.

⚠️ **Signature type 3 does not use a plain EIP-712 signature.** It uses ERC-7739 nested `TypedDataSign` wrapping plus an appended trailer for EIP-1271 verification (`_internal/actions/orders/typed_data.py`, `build_order_signature`). Hand-rolling this is a real trap — use the SDK.

⚠️ **EOA (type 0) is gated.** The docs say *"If your EOA is allowlisted for trading"* — plain EOA trading requires allowlisting, and every on-chain action (approvals, splits, merges, redemptions) costs you POL. Deposit Wallets get gasless relayer execution. **Recommend Deposit Wallet / type 3.**

The V2 signed struct (`_PROTOCOL_NAME = "Polymarket CTF Exchange"`, `version = "2"`, `verifyingContract` = the standard or negRisk exchange for that market):
```
Order(uint256 salt,address maker,address signer,uint256 tokenId,uint256 makerAmount,
      uint256 takerAmount,uint8 side,uint8 signatureType,uint256 timestamp,
      bytes32 metadata,bytes32 builder)
```
`maker` = funder (Deposit Wallet), `signer` = EOA. `side`: BUY=0, SELL=1. `expiration`, `orderType`, `postOnly`, `deferExec` ride in the wire body but are **not signed**.

---

## 3. Allowances

Source: https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/wallets-auth §Set Up Trading Approvals; addresses cross-verified against https://docs.polymarket.com/resources/contracts **and** the SDK's `polymarket/environments.py` (they match exactly).

Four approvals, from the **funder** (wallet) address:

| Token | Call | Spender |
|---|---|---|
| pUSD `0xC011a7E12a19f7B1f670d46F03B03f3342E82DFB` | `approve(spender, maxUint256)` | Standard Exchange `0xE111180000d2663C0091e4f400237545B87B996B` |
| pUSD | `approve(spender, maxUint256)` | NegRisk Exchange `0xe2222d279d744050d28e00520010520000310F59` |
| CTF `0x4D97DCd97eC945f40cF65F87097ACe5EA0476045` | `setApprovalForAll(op, true)` | Standard Exchange |
| CTF | `setApprovalForAll(op, true)` | NegRisk Exchange |

One call does all of it, idempotently: `client.setup_trading_approvals()` — *"checks existing approvals and submits only what is missing."* For Deposit Wallets these go through the relayer as a signed batch (gasless).

**Then sync the CLOB's allowance cache** — easy to miss, and orders reject without it:
```
GET /balance-allowance/update?asset_type=COLLATERAL&signature_type=3
GET /balance-allowance/update?asset_type=CONDITIONAL&token_id=<tid>&signature_type=3
```
(L2-signed; query params excluded from the signed path). Refresh `CONDITIONAL` per token before its **first sell**. Note the `signature_type=3` here is the *wallet* signature type, reusing the same enum.

The docs also note order placement *"can recover from missing allowances automatically"* — but on 5m markets you cannot afford that latency. Approve once at startup.

### negRisk on crypto up/down: **FALSE**

I checked all 24 live `*-updown-5m` / `*-updown-15m` markets on Gamma (btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge, bnb, hype, zec). **Every one is identical:**

```
negRisk = False        orderPriceMinTickSize = 0.01     orderMinSize = 5
feeSchedule = {rate: 0.07, exponent: 1, takerOnly: true, rebateRate: 0.2}
feeType = "crypto_fees_v2"
```

So they route to the **standard** exchange `0xE1111800…`. Three ways to read it per-market:
- Gamma `GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets?slug=…` → `negRisk`
- CLOB `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/neg-risk?token_id=…` → `{"neg_risk":false}`
- CLOB `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/markets/{condition_id}` → `neg_risk`

Still approve both exchanges — it's a one-time cost and negRisk is a per-market property that could change for other series.

---

## 4. Order types and the exact FAK BUY call

`OrderType = Literal["GTC","GTD","FAK","FOK"]`; `MarketOrderType = Literal["FAK","FOK"]`.

**Important asymmetry in the SDK:** `place_limit_order()` only ever emits GTC or GTD (`order_type = "GTC" if expiration is None else "GTD"` — `_internal/actions/orders/limit.py:118`). **There is no FAK/FOK limit-order helper.** A fill-and-kill must go through `place_market_order()`.

And `place_market_order()` **rejects `shares` for BUY**:
```python
if side == "BUY":
    if amount is None: raise UserInputError("amount is required for BUY market orders.")
    if shares is not None: raise UserInputError("shares must not be set for BUY market orders.")
```
`shares` is SELL-only; `max_price` is BUY-only; `min_price` is SELL-only.

### The call you asked for — FAK BUY of N shares at limit price P

```python
from decimal import Decimal
from polymarket import AsyncSecureClient

client = await AsyncSecureClient.create(
    private_key=os.environ["SIGNER_PRIVATE_KEY"],
    wallet=os.environ["POLYMARKET_WALLET_ADDRESS"],   # Deposit Wallet, != signer
)

N = Decimal("20")        # shares
P = Decimal("0.53")      # must lie on the 0.01 tick grid

resp = await client.place_market_order(
    token_id=token_id,
    side="BUY",
    amount=str(N * P),      # 10.60 — pre-fee USD notional
    max_price=str(P),       # limit; makes it a "protected" market order
    order_type="FAK",
)
if not resp.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(resp.message)
```

**Rounding — the part that will bite you.** `_compute_market_order_amounts()` with `protect_price=True`:

```python
config     = {"0.01": RoundingConfig(amount=4, price=2, size=2)}[tick]
raw_price  = round_down(P, 2)
raw_maker  = round_down(amount, 2)          # ← notional truncated to 2 dp
raw_taker  = raw_maker / raw_price          # ← implied shares
# if >4 dp: round_up to 8 dp, then round_up to 4 dp (round_up because protected)
```

Consequence: **you only get exactly N shares when `N × P` is exact to 2 decimals.** With P on the 0.01 grid, any integer N works. Counter-example: `N=7.5, P=0.53` → `3.975` truncates to `3.97` → taker = `7.4906` shares, not 7.5.

→ **Use integer N.** Also enforce `N ≥ 5` and `N × P ≥ 5` (see the min-order-size ambiguity below).

Tick grid is validated client-side by `validate_price_on_tick_grid()`: price must be an integer multiple of tick **and** within `[tick, 1 − tick]` — so `0.01 ≤ P ≤ 0.99` here. Server-side rejection reads `Price (100) breaks minimum tick size rule: 0.1`.

Full rounding table (`_internal/actions/orders/context.py`) — note the SDK adds `0.005` and `0.0025` that py-clob-client never had:

| tick | amount dp | price dp | size dp |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| **0.01** | **4** | **2** | **2** |
| 0.005 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| 0.0025 | 6 | 4 | 2 |
| 0.001 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| 0.0001 | 6 | 4 | 2 |

**GTD gotcha:** GTD orders expire *one minute before* the stated time, and expiration must be ≥3 minutes out or it's rejected. Set `now + 60 + N`. Minimum practical lifetime ≈2 minutes — **GTD is unusable on 5m markets.** Use FAK/FOK.

**Split create/post:** `create_market_order(...) -> SignedOrder` then `post_order(signed)`, or `post_orders([...])` for batches of 1–15.

⚠️ **`orderMinSize` is ambiguous.** The Gamma field reference says *"Minimum order size in USDC"* (market-details.md:470), but the CLOB returns `minimum_order_size: 5` / `mos: 5` and the live book contains 5-size resting orders at `0.4` (= $2 notional), which is inconsistent with a $5 floor. `rewardsMinSize` is explicitly documented "in shares." **Satisfy both interpretations** (N ≥ 5 shares AND N×P ≥ $5) until you've probed it empirically.

---

## 5. Fills and latency

### Create-order response
`POST /order` → `{success, orderID, status, makingAmount, takingAmount, errorMsg}`, plus `transactionsHashes[]` and `tradeIDs[]` **when `status == "matched"`**. Python: `AcceptedOrder(ok, order_id, status, making_amount, taking_amount, trade_ids, transactions_hashes)` / `RejectedOrder(ok, code, message)`.

`status` ∈ `live | matched | delayed` (`unmatched` also appears in the lifecycle doc for post-delay resting).

### ⚠️ 250 ms taker delay — this applies to your markets

From https://docs.polymarket.com/concepts/order-lifecycle:

> **Taker delay:** used on selected crypto and finance up/down markets. The order is held for 250 ms, then validation runs again and the order is matched or placed on the book. The API waits for this hold and returns the final order result. To check a specific market, call `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/clob-markets/{condition_id}` and look for `itode: true`.

I confirmed `"itode": true` on the live BTC 5m market. So:
- Every marketable order eats a **250 ms hold** before matching, and `POST /order` blocks for it.
- **The order cannot be canceled during the hold.**
- If balance/allowance/risk checks fail when the hold expires, it's rejected rather than matched.

For 5m markets this is a material adverse-selection window — price can move against you inside the hold with no ability to pull.

### Trade status progression
`MATCHED_NOT_BROADCASTED → MATCHED → MINED → CONFIRMED` (terminal), or `RETRYING → FAILED` (terminal). Only `CONFIRMED` and `FAILED` are terminal; **a tx hash seen at MINED can still be replaced on retry** (per the SDK's own comment in `settlement.py`).

### Confirmation paths
1. **Synchronous** — `tradeIDs` + `transactionsHashes` in the POST response when `matched`. Fastest signal that you got a fill.
2. **`client.wait_for_order_fill_settlement(resp, timeout_s=30.0)`** — polls `/data/trades?id=<trade_id>` every **250 ms** until every trade is `CONFIRMED`/`FAILED`. Default timeout 30 s (`DEFAULT_SETTLEMENT_TIMEOUT_S`). Raises `TransactionFailedError` if all fills failed.
3. **User WebSocket** `wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com/ws/user` — subscribe immediately on connect with `{"auth":{"apiKey","secret","passphrase"}, "type":"user"}`, optional `"markets":[condition_id]`. **App-level heartbeat: send text frame `PING` every 10 s, server replies `PONG`.** Server may close an unsubscribed connection. Python: `async with await client.subscribe(UserSpec()) as stream`.
4. **Polling** — `GET /data/order/{id}`, `GET /data/orders`, `GET /data/trades`.

**Latency guidance.** I could not measure match→confirm directly (the Data API `timestamp` field is the *settlement block* timestamp, not match time — all 40 deltas I computed were exactly 0). Grounded estimate: 250 ms taker hold + operator broadcast + **measured Polygon block time 1.50 s** (over the last 500 blocks) + finality. Expect `matched` in the HTTP response in well under a second, `CONFIRMED` on the order of a few seconds. The SDK's 30 s default timeout is the design envelope, not the typical case. **Trade off the synchronous `matched` response; treat `CONFIRMED` as bookkeeping.** After any WS reconnect, re-read open orders and recent trades — the stream does not replay.

---

## 6. Fees — verified on-chain

Docs: https://docs.polymarket.com/trading/fees

```
fee = C × rate × (p × (1 − p))^exponent        # C = shares, p = price, in USDC/pUSD
```
Crypto: **rate 0.07, exponent 1, takerOnly true, maker rebate 0.20**. Makers never pay. Fees round to 5 dp; minimum 0.00001.

**Authoritative per-market source** — `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/clob-markets/{condition_id}` (this is exactly what the SDK calls, `market_data.py:88`). Live response for the BTC 5m market:
```json
{"mos":5, "mts":0.01, "mbf":1000, "tbf":1000, "ao":true, "itode":true,
 "fd":{"r":0.07,"e":1,"to":true},
 "r":{"mi":50,"ma":4.5,"moas":30}, "t":[...], "c":"0x..."}
```
`fd` = fee descriptor (`r`=rate, `e`=exponent, `to`=takerOnly). Gamma exposes the same as `feeSchedule`.

### ⚠️ `feeRateBps` is a V1 fossil — do not use it
- The V2 signed order struct **has no `feeRateBps` field at all**. *"Fees are set by the protocol and applied at match time — you don't include fee information in your orders."*
- `GET /fee-rate?token_id=…` returns `{"base_fee":1000}` and Gamma returns `takerBaseFee: 1000` / `makerBaseFee: 1000`. **These are stale and inconsistent with the actual 0.07 schedule** — 1000 bps would be 10%, the real effective charge at p=0.50 is 3.5% of notional. Ignore them.
- `fee_rate_bps` on trade/WS payloads is a legacy passthrough (docs example shows `"0"`). Don't reconcile against it.

### How the fee is actually applied — decoded from real fills

**BUY (taker) — fee charged in pUSD *on top of* notional; share count is NOT reduced.**

Tx `0xe669c39a513d955d93a05739db46a298da5d3dadf9b96a70669c61bdc5e10ba3` (BTC up/down 5m), trader `0x251c1a28…`:
- pUSD out: **36.717320**
- CTF shares in: **60.000000** (full amount)
- Separate pUSD fee transfer from the exchange: **1.012020**

Check: 60 × 0.5950883 = 35.705300 notional; 36.717320 − 35.705300 = 1.012020. Formula predicts 60 × 0.07 × 0.59508833 × 0.40491167 = **1.012016**. ✓

**SELL (taker) — fee deducted from proceeds; full shares delivered.** DOGE up/down 5m: 0.02 shares @ 0.32 → notional 0.006400, predicted fee 0.000305, **received 0.0061**. ✓ (A non-crypto control at rate 0.05 also matched exactly: 5 @ 0.20 → received 0.96, fee 0.04.)

The Data API `price` is the pure execution VWAP, **fee-exclusive**.

### Economic note for 5m up/down

## 7. Redemption

**USDC does not arrive automatically by default** — you must redeem. Three options:

1. **`client.redeem_positions(condition_id=...)`** — yes, the new SDK supports it (`py-clob-client` had **no** redeem/merge/split at all). No amount parameter; redeems both outcome balances. Returns a transaction handle with `.wait()`.
2. **Direct contract call** via the collateral adapter (not the raw CTF):
   - `CtfCollateralAdapter` `0xAdA100Db00Ca00073811820692005400218FcE1f` when `negRisk == false` ← **your case**
   - `NegRiskCtfCollateralAdapter` `0xadA2005600Dec949baf300f4C6120000bDB6eAab` when true
   ```solidity
   redeemPositions(address collateralToken, bytes32 parentCollectionId,
                   bytes32 conditionId, uint256[] indexSets)
   ```
   with `collateralToken = 0xC011a7E1…` (pUSD), `parentCollectionId = bytes32(0)`, `indexSets = [1,2]`. The adapter burns your ERC-1155s through CTF, receives the released USDC.e, wraps to pUSD, returns pUSD.
3. **Auto-Redeem** — a UI toggle (Settings → Trading) that redeems resolved winnings automatically after the dispute period. Community-reported, not in the developer docs, and **no documented API surface** — treat as unavailable programmatically. There is an on-chain `AutoRedeemer` at `0xa1200000d0002264C9a1698e001292D00E1b00af` (undocumented).

**No redemption deadline** — winning tokens stay redeemable indefinitely, so you can batch redemptions rather than firing one per 5-minute market.

**Prerequisite:** the collateral adapter must be approved to move your outcome tokens (separate from the exchange approvals in §3).

I pulled real `PayoutRedemption` events from CTF `0x4D97DCd9…` on Polygon and read the receipts. Volume is enormous — **2,313 redemptions across 744 txs in ~120 blocks (~3 min)**, consistent with the 5m/15m crypto series churning.

## 8. Rate limits

**Two independent layers.**

### (a) Per-signer token buckets — https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/trading-rate-limits

⚠️ **Version-dependent:** *"Beginning July 24, 2026, the limiter will run in warning mode for two weeks. Requests will continue to be processed during this period."* Two weeks from July 24 = **~August 7, 2026 — that has passed as of today (Aug 12)**, but the doc says Polymarket *"will announce when live enforcement begins"* and gives no confirmed date. **Assume enforcement is live and instrument for it.**

Separate order and cancel buckets per signer address. Token costs: `POST /order` = 1; `POST /orders` = batch size; `DELETE /order` = 1; `DELETE /orders` = #ids; `DELETE /cancel-all` and `/cancel-market-orders` = 1 **plus one per order actually canceled** (debited after the fact, can push the bucket negative).

| Tier | 30d volume | Order rate/s | Order burst | Cancel rate/s | Cancel burst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | — | **40** | **60** | **80** | **120** |
| Copper | $30k+ | 60 | 90 | 120 | 180 |
| Bronze | $50k+ | 80 | 120 | 160 | 240 |
| Silver | $100k+ | 200 | 300 | 400 | 600 |
| Gold | $500k+ | 400 | 600 | 800 | 1,200 |
| Platinum | $2.5M+ | 450 | 675 | 900 | 1,350 |
| Diamond | $5M+ | 525 | 787 | 1,050 | 1,575 |
| Elite | $10M+ | 600 | 900 | 1,200 | 1,800 |

Burst = max bucket capacity; `burst_seconds = burst / rate_per_sec`. **Batches are all-or-nothing**: rejected entirely unless the bucket holds tokens for every entry, and a batch costing more than burst capacity can *never* be admitted — split it. Tiers key off the **maker wallet's** 30-day volume (even when that differs from the signer), refreshed every 3 hours.

Headers: `Poly-RateLimit-Remaining` (can go negative after cancel-all), `Poly-RateLimit-Reset`, `Poly-RateLimit-Tier`, plus `Retry-After` on 429 and `Poly-RateLimit-Warning: true` while in warning mode. **Monitor `Poly-RateLimit-Warning` now** — it tells you what would be rejected once enforcement flips. `Poly-RateLimit-Reset` is when enough tokens exist for *the attempted request*, not a full bucket.

### (b) Cloudflare IP limits — https://docs.polymarket.com/api-reference/rate-limits
Throttled (queued), not rejected. `POST /order`: 5,000/10s burst, 120,000/10min sustained. `POST /orders`: 2,000/10s, 21,000/10min. `/book` and `/price`: 1,500/10s. Gamma `/markets`: 300/10s. Data API `/trades`: 200/10s. These are far above the per-signer buckets — **the token bucket binds first.**
